en.title: Seen in the Desert
story: Hagar was an Egyptian servant in Abraham and Sarah’s household. Sarah treated her harshly, and Hagar ran away into the desert. She was a foreigner, a servant and a runaway: about as forgotten as a person could feel.

By a spring of water on the road to Egypt, the angel of the Lord found her. Notice the word ‘found’. Hagar wasn’t looking for God, but God was looking for her. ‘Hagar, slave of Sarai, where have you come from, and where are you going?’ God knew her name and her story.
God told her that He had heard her misery. He promised that her son, Ishmael, would grow up and have many descendants. Ishmael’s name means ‘God hears’.
Hagar responded by giving God a name: ‘You are the God who sees me.’ In Hebrew, El Roi. She is the only person in the Bible who gave God a name, and it came from her own experience of being seen.

Years later, Hagar and Ishmael were sent away and their water ran out. Hagar couldn’t bear to watch her son die, so she sat a distance away and cried. ‘God heard the boy crying,’ and He opened her eyes to see a well. The God who sees is also the God who hears.

You might sometimes feel invisible: at school, among friends, even at home. But you are never unseen by God. He knows exactly where you are and how you feel. And just like Hagar, you can talk to Him about it. He is listening.

verse.text: You are the God who sees me.

lessons: God sees and knows each person, especially those who feel forgotten.
God goes looking for people who run away and feel alone.
The God who sees is also the God who hears our cries.
questions: Why do you think Hagar felt so alone?
What do the names ‘El Roi’ and ‘Ishmael’ tell us about God?
When do you feel unseen? How could knowing God sees you help?
en.listen: Be still for one minute. Ask God: ‘What do you see when you look at me?’ Listen, and write down what you sense. God’s words will always be kind and true.
prayer: El Roi, you are the God who sees me.
Right now I feel…
Thank you that you see me and hear me.

mission.text: Tomorrow, notice someone who might feel invisible, and do something kind so they know they’re seen.

en.journal: Write about a time you felt invisible. Then write what El Roi would say to you in that moment.

af.title: Raakgesien in die Woestyn
story: Hagar was ’n Egiptiese diensmeisie in Abraham en Sara se huishouding. Sara het haar hard behandel, en Hagar het die woestyn in weggehardloop. Sy was ’n vreemdeling, ’n diensmeisie en ’n weghardloper: omtrent so vergete as wat ’n mens kan voel.

By ’n fontein op die pad na Egipte het die engel van die Here haar gekry. Let op die woord ‘gekry’. Hagar het nie na God gesoek nie, maar God het na haar gesoek. ‘Hagar, slavin van Sarai, waar kom jy vandaan, en waarheen gaan jy?’ God het haar naam en haar storie geken.
God het vir haar gesê dat Hy van haar ellende gehoor het. Hy het belowe dat haar seun, Ismael, sou grootword en baie nakomelinge sou hê. Ismael se naam beteken ‘God hoor’.

Hagar het geantwoord deur God ’n naam te gee: ‘U is die God wat my sien.’ In Hebreeus, El Roi. Sy is die enigste mens in die Bybel wat God ’n naam gegee het, en dit het uit haar eie ervaring gekom van om raakgesien te word.

Jare later is Hagar en Ismael weggestuur en hulle water het opgeraak. Hagar kon nie verdra om haar seun te sien sterf nie, toe gaan sit sy ’n entjie weg en huil. ‘God het die seun hoor huil,’ en Hy het haar oë oopgemaak om ’n put te sien. Die God wat sien, is ook die God wat hoor.

Jy voel dalk soms onsigbaar: by die skool, tussen maats, selfs by die huis. Maar God sien jou altyd. Hy weet presies waar jy is en hoe jy voel. En net soos Hagar kan jy met Hom daaroor praat. Hy luister.

verse.text: U is die God wat my sien.

lessons: God sien en ken elke mens, veral die wat vergete voel.
God gaan soek na mense wat weghardloop en alleen voel.
Die God wat sien, is ook die God wat ons hoor roep.
questions: Hoekom dink jy het Hagar so alleen gevoel?
Wat sê die name ‘El Roi’ en ‘Ismael’ vir ons oor God?
Wanneer voel jy onsigbaar? Hoe kan dit help om te weet God sien jou?
af.listen: Wees een minuut lank stil. Vra God: ‘Wat sien U as U na my kyk?’ Luister, en skryf neer wat jy aanvoel. God se woorde sal altyd liefdevol en waar wees.
prayer: El Roi, U is die God wat my sien.
Op die oomblik voel ek…
Dankie dat U my sien en hoor.

mission.text: Kyk môre na iemand wat dalk onsigbaar voel, en doen iets gaafs sodat hulle weet hulle word raakgesien.

af.journal: Skryf oor ’n keer toe jy onsigbaar gevoel het. Skryf dan wat El Roi op daardie oomblik vir jou sou sê.

en.title: The God Who Sees Me
story: Genesis 16 is an uncomfortable chapter. Sarah, unable to have children, gives her Egyptian servant Hagar to Abraham so that Hagar can have a child for her. It was a common custom then, but it was not God’s plan, and it goes badly. Hagar becomes pregnant, tension explodes, and Sarah mistreats her until Hagar flees into the desert.

Think about Hagar’s position: a foreign slave woman, pregnant, alone, with no rights and no protection. She had been used by others and then pushed out. In her world, she was the least important person in the story.

But read verse 7: ‘The angel of the Lord found Hagar near a spring in the desert.’ The first time an angel appears in the Bible, he comes not to a king or a patriarch, but to a runaway slave. God addresses her by name and asks two questions: ‘Where have you come from, and where are you going?’ God invites her to tell her story.

He doesn’t remove all her difficulties; He tells her to go back. But He gives her a promise, a future and a son whose name, Ishmael, means ‘God hears’. And Hagar responds with theology from her own experience: ‘You are the God who sees me… I have now seen the One who sees me.’
In chapter 21, abandoned again with Ishmael, she sits down to cry, and ‘God heard the boy crying’. He opened her eyes to a well that had been there all along.

What does this teach us? God is not only the God of the important people in the story. He notices the overlooked, the used and the hurting. If you have ever felt used, excluded or invisible, Hagar’s God sees you too. And He calls His followers to see the Hagars around them, and to treat them the way He does.

verse.text: You are the God who sees me… I have now seen the One who sees me.

lessons: God sees and cares for the overlooked, the used and the hurting.
God invites us to bring Him our whole story: where we have come from and where we are going.
God’s followers are called to see the ‘Hagars’ around them.
questions: What does it reveal about God that the first angel in the Bible appears to a runaway slave?
Have you ever felt used, excluded or invisible? What does El Roi say to that?
Who is a ‘Hagar’ in your world who needs to be seen?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Answer God’s two questions honestly in writing: ‘Where have you come from? Where are you going?’ Then ask Him what He wants to say to you.
prayer: El Roi, thank you that you see me.
This is where I have come from, and where I feel I am going: …
Open my eyes to see others the way you see them.

mission.text: This week, make a point of including someone who is usually on the edge: in a conversation, a game or a group.

en.journal: Write about the ‘well’ Hagar didn’t see until God opened her eyes. Is there something good in your life you haven’t noticed? Ask God to open your eyes.

af.title: Die God wat My Sien
story: Genesis 16 is ’n ongemaklike hoofstuk. Sara, wat nie kinders kon kry nie, gee haar Egiptiese diensmeisie Hagar vir Abraham sodat Hagar vir haar ’n kind kan hê. Dit was toe ’n algemene gebruik, maar dit was nie God se plan nie, en dit loop sleg af. Hagar word swanger, spanning ontplof, en Sara mishandel haar totdat Hagar die woestyn in vlug.

Dink aan Hagar se posisie: ’n vreemde slavevrou, swanger, alleen, sonder regte en sonder beskerming. Sy is deur ander gebruik en toe uitgestoot. In haar wêreld was sy die onbelangrikste persoon in die storie.

Maar lees vers 7: ‘Die engel van die Here het Hagar by ’n fontein in die woestyn gekry.’ Die eerste keer dat ’n engel in die Bybel verskyn, kom hy nie na ’n koning of ’n aartsvader nie, maar na ’n weggeloopte slavin. God spreek haar op haar naam aan en vra twee vrae: ‘Waar kom jy vandaan, en waarheen gaan jy?’ God nooi haar om haar storie te vertel.

Hy neem nie al haar probleme weg nie; Hy sê sy moet teruggaan. Maar Hy gee haar ’n belofte, ’n toekoms en ’n seun wie se naam, Ismael, ‘God hoor’ beteken. En Hagar antwoord met teologie uit haar eie ervaring: ‘U is die God wat my sien… Ek het nou die Een gesien wat my sien.’
In hoofstuk 21, weer saam met Ismael verlaat, gaan sit sy om te huil, en ‘God het die seun hoor huil’. Hy het haar oë oopgemaak vir ’n put wat al die tyd daar was.

Wat leer dit ons? God is nie net die God van die belangrike mense in die storie nie. Hy sien die oor-die-hoof-gesienes, die gebruiktes en die wat seerkry raak. As jy al ooit gebruik, uitgesluit of onsigbaar gevoel het, sien Hagar se God jou ook. En Hy roep sy volgelinge om die Hagars rondom hulle raak te sien, en om hulle te behandel soos Hy doen.

verse.text: U is die God wat my sien… Ek het nou die Een gesien wat my sien.

lessons: God sien en sorg vir die oor-die-hoof-gesienes, die gebruiktes en die wat seerkry.
God nooi ons om ons hele storie na Hom te bring: waar ons vandaan kom en waarheen ons gaan.
God se volgelinge word geroep om die ‘Hagars’ rondom hulle raak te sien.
questions: Wat wys dit oor God dat die eerste engel in die Bybel aan ’n weggeloopte slavin verskyn?
Het jy al ooit gebruik, uitgesluit of onsigbaar gevoel? Wat sê El Roi daaroor?
Wie is ’n ‘Hagar’ in jou wêreld wat raakgesien moet word?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Beantwoord God se twee vrae eerlik op skrif: ‘Waar kom jy vandaan? Waarheen gaan jy?’ Vra Hom dan wat Hy vir jou wil sê.
prayer: El Roi, dankie dat U my sien.
Dit is waar ek vandaan kom, en waarheen ek voel ek gaan: …
Maak my oë oop om ander te sien soos U hulle sien.

mission.text: Maak hierdie week ’n punt daarvan om iemand in te sluit wat gewoonlik op die kantlyn is: in ’n gesprek, ’n speletjie of ’n groep.

af.journal: Skryf oor die ‘put’ wat Hagar nie gesien het totdat God haar oë oopgemaak het nie. Is daar iets goeds in jou lewe wat jy nie raakgesien het nie? Vra God om jou oë oop te maak.

en.title: God Sees Me
story: Hagar and her little boy were alone in the hot desert.
Their water was all gone. They were thirsty and sad.
But God saw them! An angel said, ‘Don’t be afraid.’
God showed Hagar a well full of cool water. Glug, glug!
Hagar said, ‘You are the God who sees me!’

en.action: Cover your eyes with your hands, then open them wide and say: ‘God sees me!’
lessons: God always sees me.
questions: Where are you right now? God sees you there!
prayer: Thank you, God,
that you always see me. Amen.

lessons: God sien my altyd.
questions: Waar is jy nou? God sien jou daar!

trait.en: God guides my steps
trait.af: God lei my treë

en.title: A Prayer at the Well
story: Abraham wanted his son Isaac to marry someone who would share his faith in God. So he sent his oldest, most trusted servant on a journey of hundreds of kilometres back to his relatives, with ten camels and many gifts.

When the servant arrived at the town well in the evening, he faced an impossible task: how do you choose the right person out of a whole town? So he did the wisest thing: he prayed. ‘Lord, God of my master Abraham, make me successful today.’ He asked God for a specific sign: the right young woman would offer water not only to him, but to his camels too.
That was a big ask. A thirsty camel can drink up to a hundred litres of water, and there were ten of them! Whoever did that would be showing extraordinary kindness and hard work.

‘Before he had finished praying, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder.’ When the servant asked for a drink, she said, ‘Drink, my lord… I’ll draw water for your camels too, until they have had enough.’ She ran back and forth to the well until the job was done.
The servant watched in amazement, then bowed down and worshipped: ‘Praise be to the Lord… As for me, the Lord has led me on the journey.’

God still guides His children. Sometimes He answers dramatically; more often He leads step by step as we pray, trust Him and keep walking. Notice too that God used Rebekah’s ordinary kindness as part of His plan. Your kindness can be part of someone else’s answered prayer.

verse.text: Trust in the Lord with all your heart… and He will make your paths straight.

lessons: God guides us when we pray and trust Him.
God sometimes answers prayer before we have even finished praying!
Our everyday kindness can be part of God’s plan for someone else.
questions: What sign did the servant ask God for? Why was it such a good test of character?
How did Rebekah go beyond what was asked?
What decision do you need God’s guidance for right now?
en.listen: Bring God a decision you need to make. Ask: ‘Lord, how do you want to guide me in this?’ Listen quietly, and write down what you sense.

mission.text: Tomorrow, go beyond what is asked: when someone asks for a little help, give a lot.

en.journal: Write down a decision you are facing. Write a prayer asking God to guide you, and leave space to write how He answers.

af.title: ’n Gebed by die Put
story: Abraham wou hê sy seun Isak moet trou met iemand wat sy geloof in God sou deel. Toe stuur hy sy oudste, mees betroubare dienskneg op ’n reis van honderde kilometers terug na sy familie, met tien kamele en baie geskenke.

Toe die dienskneg saans by die dorp se put aankom, het hy voor ’n onmoontlike taak gestaan: hoe kies jy die regte persoon uit ’n hele dorp? Toe het hy die wysste ding gedoen: hy het gebid. ‘Here, God van my meester Abraham, laat dit vandag vir my goed gaan.’ Hy het God vir ’n spesifieke teken gevra: die regte jong vrou sou nie net vir hom water aanbied nie, maar vir sy kamele ook.
Dit was ’n groot versoek. ’n Dors kameel kan tot honderd liter water drink, en daar was tien van hulle! Wie dit ook al doen, sou buitengewone goedheid en harde werk wys.

‘Voordat hy klaar gebid het, het Rebekka met haar kruik op haar skouer uitgekom.’ Toe die dienskneg vir ’n drinkie vra, het sy gesê: ‘Drink, meneer… Ek sal ook vir jou kamele water skep, totdat hulle genoeg gehad het.’ Sy het heen en weer na die put gehardloop totdat die werk klaar was.
Die dienskneg het verwonderd gekyk, en toe gebuig en aanbid: ‘Prys die Here… Wat my betref, die Here het my op die reis gelei.’

God lei vandag nog sy kinders. Soms antwoord Hy dramaties; meestal lei Hy tree vir tree terwyl ons bid, Hom vertrou en aanhou loop. Let ook op dat God Rebekka se gewone goedheid as deel van sy plan gebruik het. Jou goedheid kan deel wees van iemand anders se beantwoorde gebed.

verse.text: Vertrou op die Here met jou hele hart… en Hy sal jou paaie gelyk maak.

lessons: God lei ons as ons bid en Hom vertrou.
God antwoord soms gebed nog voordat ons klaar gebid het!
Ons alledaagse goedheid kan deel wees van God se plan vir iemand anders.
questions: Watter teken het die dienskneg God voor gevra? Hoekom was dit so ’n goeie toets van karakter?
Hoe het Rebekka meer gedoen as wat gevra is?
Vir watter besluit het jy nou God se leiding nodig?
af.listen: Bring vir God ’n besluit wat jy moet neem. Vra: ‘Here, hoe wil U my hierin lei?’ Luister stil, en skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Here, dankie dat U u kinders lei.
Lei my asseblief met…
Help my om gaaf te wees soos Rebekka, selfs as dit harde werk is.

mission.text: Doen môre meer as wat gevra word: as iemand vir ’n bietjie hulp vra, gee baie.

af.journal: Skryf ’n besluit neer waarvoor jy staan. Skryf ’n gebed waarin jy God vra om jou te lei, en laat plek om te skryf hoe Hy antwoord.

en.title: Guidance and Character
story: Genesis 24 is the longest chapter in Genesis, and it is entirely about one question: how does God guide? Abraham’s servant has a huge responsibility: find a wife for Isaac from Abraham’s relatives, far away. He has no map, no app and no idea who he is looking for.

Look at what he does. First, he prays specifically. He asks for a sign that is really a test of character: the right woman would generously offer to water ten thirsty camels, which would be at least an hour of exhausting work. He wasn’t asking God for a random coincidence. He was asking God to show him someone with a servant heart.

Second, he watches and waits. Verse 21 says ‘without saying a word, the man watched her closely to learn whether or not the Lord had made his journey successful’. Guidance often involves patient observation, not rushing to conclusions.
Third, when God answers, he worships immediately: ‘Praise be to the Lord… I have been on the journey, and the Lord has led me.’

Then notice Rebekah. She is not a passive character. When asked, ‘Will you go with this man?’ she answers, ‘I will go.’ It took courage to leave everything for a family she had never met, trusting that God was in it.

How does God guide us today? Mainly through His Word, which shows us His will in most situations. Through prayer and the peace of the Holy Spirit. Through wise people around us. And sometimes through circumstances that line up in remarkable ways. Usually guidance isn’t a dramatic voice telling us exactly what to do. It is God leading people who are walking closely with Him, one step at a time.
Also notice that character mattered more than appearance. The servant wasn’t looking for the most beautiful or popular girl, but the kindest. God still values that most.

verse.text: In all your ways submit to Him, and He will make your paths straight.

lessons: God guides people who pray, watch patiently and walk closely with Him.
God usually guides through His Word, prayer, wise people and circumstances.
Character, like a servant heart, matters more to God than appearance or popularity.
questions: What three things did the servant do to seek God’s guidance?
Why was Rebekah’s ‘I will go’ an act of faith?
What helps you know God’s guidance? What makes it harder?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Bring God a choice you are facing. Pray, then watch and wait quietly. Write down any thought, verse or sense of peace that comes.
prayer: Lord, I want to walk closely with you so you can guide me.
Please lead me in my decision about…
Give me a servant heart like Rebekah’s.

mission.text: Before any big choice this week, follow the servant’s pattern: pray specifically, watch patiently, and thank God when He leads.

en.journal: List the ways God has guided you in the past. Which way does He seem to use most in your life?

af.title: Leiding en Karakter
story: Genesis 24 is die langste hoofstuk in Genesis, en dit gaan heeltemal oor een vraag: hoe lei God? Abraham se dienskneg het ’n groot verantwoordelikheid: kry ’n vrou vir Isak uit Abraham se familie, ver weg. Hy het geen kaart nie, geen toep nie, en geen idee na wie hy soek nie.

Kyk wat hy doen. Eerstens bid hy spesifiek. Hy vra vir ’n teken wat eintlik ’n toets van karakter is: die regte vrou sou vrygewig aanbied om tien dors kamele water te gee, wat ten minste ’n uur se uitputtende werk sou wees. Hy het God nie vir ’n lukrake toeval gevra nie. Hy het God gevra om hom iemand met ’n diensbare hart te wys.

Tweedens hou hy dop en wag. Vers 21 sê ‘sonder om ’n woord te sê, het die man haar noukeurig dopgehou om te weet of die Here sy reis laat slaag het of nie’. Leiding vra dikwels geduldige waarneming, nie om haastig gevolgtrekkings te maak nie.
Derdens, toe God antwoord, aanbid hy dadelik: ‘Prys die Here… Ek was op die reis, en die Here het my gelei.’

Let dan op Rebekka. Sy is nie ’n passiewe karakter nie. Toe sy gevra word: ‘Sal jy saam met hierdie man gaan?’ antwoord sy: ‘Ek sal gaan.’ Dit het moed gekos om alles agter te laat vir ’n familie wat sy nog nooit ontmoet het nie, en te vertrou dat God daarin was.

Hoe lei God ons vandag? Hoofsaaklik deur sy Woord, wat ons in die meeste situasies sy wil wys. Deur gebed en die vrede van die Heilige Gees. Deur wyse mense rondom ons. En soms deur omstandighede wat op merkwaardige maniere inmekaarpas. Gewoonlik is leiding nie ’n dramatiese stem wat ons presies vertel wat om te doen nie. Dit is God wat mense lei wat naby Hom lewe, een tree op ’n slag.
Let ook op dat karakter meer saak gemaak het as voorkoms. Die dienskneg het nie na die mooiste of gewildste meisie gesoek nie, maar na die gaafste. God ag dit vandag nog die meeste.

verse.text: Erken Hom in alles wat jy doen, en Hy sal jou paaie gelyk maak.

lessons: God lei mense wat bid, geduldig dophou en naby Hom lewe.
God lei gewoonlik deur sy Woord, gebed, wyse mense en omstandighede.
Karakter, soos ’n diensbare hart, maak vir God meer saak as voorkoms of gewildheid.
questions: Watter drie dinge het die dienskneg gedoen om God se leiding te soek?
Hoekom was Rebekka se ‘Ek sal gaan’ ’n daad van geloof?
Wat help jou om God se leiding te ken? Wat maak dit moeiliker?

prayer: Here, ek wil naby U lewe sodat U my kan lei.
Lei my asseblief in my besluit oor…
Gee my ’n diensbare hart soos Rebekka s’n.

Hy het gebid: ‘God, wys my asseblief die regte meisie vir Isak.’
By die put het gawe Rebekka vir hom water gegee, en vir die kamele ook! Slurp, slurp!

God wys vir ons die pad.

questions: Hoeveel kamele kan jy tel?

wys my asseblief die pad. Amen.

en.title: The Girl at the Well
story: Abraham was very old, and he wanted to find a good wife for his son Isaac. So he sent his most trusted servant on a long journey, with ten camels loaded with gifts.

When the servant reached a town far away, he stopped by a well. It was evening, and the girls of the town were coming to fetch water. The servant didn’t know what to do, so he prayed: ‘Lord, please show me the right girl. Let her be the one who offers water to me and to my camels too.’

Before he had even finished praying, a young woman called Rebekah came with a jar on her shoulder. The servant asked for a drink, and she said, ‘Drink! And I will draw water for your camels too!’ Camels drink LOTS of water. Rebekah ran back and forth to the well again and again until all ten camels had finished.
The servant bowed down and thanked God. God had led him exactly to the right person. Rebekah agreed to go home with him and marry Isaac.
When we don’t know which way to go, we can pray, just like the servant. God loves to guide His children.

verse.text: Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and He will show you the way.

lessons: God guides us when we ask Him.
God answers prayer, sometimes very quickly!
Being kind and helpful, like Rebekah, makes God smile.
questions: What did the servant pray for?
How was Rebekah kind?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you lead me.
When I don’t know what to do,
please show me the way. Amen.

af.title: Die Meisie by die Put
story: Abraham was baie oud, en hy wou ’n goeie vrou vir sy seun Isak kry. Toe stuur hy sy mees betroubare dienskneg op ’n lang reis, met tien kamele gelaai met geskenke.

Toe die dienskneg by ’n dorp ver weg aankom, het hy by ’n put stilgehou. Dit was aand, en die meisies van die dorp het gekom om water te skep. Die dienskneg het nie geweet wat om te doen nie, toe bid hy: ‘Here, wys my asseblief die regte meisie. Laat sy die een wees wat vir my en vir my kamele ook water aanbied.’

Voordat hy eers klaar gebid het, het ’n jong vrou met die naam Rebekka met ’n kruik op haar skouer gekom. Die dienskneg het vir ’n drinkie gevra, en sy het gesê: ‘Drink! En ek sal vir jou kamele ook water skep!’ Kamele drink BAIE water. Rebekka het heen en weer na die put gehardloop, keer op keer, totdat al tien kamele klaar gedrink het.
Die dienskneg het gebuig en God gedank. God het hom presies na die regte persoon gelei. Rebekka het ingestem om saam met hom huis toe te gaan en met Isak te trou.
As ons nie weet watter pad om te loop nie, kan ons bid, net soos die dienskneg. God lei graag sy kinders.

verse.text: Vertrou op die Here met jou hele hart, en Hy sal vir jou die pad wys.

lessons: God lei ons as ons Hom vra.
God antwoord gebed, soms baie vinnig!
Om gaaf en hulpvaardig te wees, soos Rebekka, laat God glimlag.
questions: Waarvoor het die dienskneg gebid?
Hoe was Rebekka gaaf?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U my lei.
As ek nie weet wat om te doen nie,
wys my asseblief die pad. Amen.

mission.text: As jy môre iets moet kies, stop en vra God om jou te help om goed te kies.

trait.en: God makes room for me
trait.af: God maak vir my plek

en.title: The Peacemaker’s Wells
story: Isaac doesn’t get as many stories as his father Abraham or his son Jacob, but Genesis 26 shows us something special about him: he was a peacemaker.

God blessed Isaac so much that his crops produced a hundred times what he planted, and his flocks and herds grew huge. That made the Philistines jealous. They filled in his father’s old wells with earth, and the king told him to move away.

In that dry land, wells were worth more than gold. When Isaac’s servants dug a new well and found fresh water, the local herdsmen argued: ‘The water is ours!’ Isaac named it Esek, which means ‘argument’, and moved on. They dug another, and the herders quarrelled again. He named it Sitnah, ‘opposition’, and moved on again.
They dug a third well, and this time no one argued. Isaac called it Rehoboth, ‘room’, and said, ‘Now the Lord has given us room and we will flourish in the land.’

That night God appeared to him: ‘Do not be afraid, for I am with you; I will bless you.’ Isaac built an altar and worshipped. Soon afterwards, the very king who had sent him away came to make a peace treaty, saying, ‘We saw clearly that the Lord was with you.’

Isaac could have fought for his rights. Instead, he trusted God to provide. His peacemaking didn’t make him a loser; it made room for God to bless him, and even won over his enemies. When you choose peace, you are trusting that God is big enough to look after you.

verse.text: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.

lessons: Peacemakers trust God instead of fighting for everything.
God makes room for His children when they trust Him.
A peaceful life can win over even our opponents.
questions: What do the names Esek, Sitnah and Rehoboth mean? Why do you think Isaac chose them?
Why might the king have changed his mind about Isaac?
Where is a situation where you could choose peace instead of an argument?
en.listen: Be still and ask God: ‘Is there an argument you want me to walk away from, or a peace you want me to make?’ Listen and write down what you sense.
prayer: Lord, thank you that you make room for me.
Help me to be a peacemaker with…
I trust you to take care of me.

mission.text: This week, when an argument starts, choose to be the first to calm it down.

en.journal: Draw three wells and label them Esek, Sitnah and Rehoboth. Next to each, write about a time in your life that feels like that well.

af.title: Die Vredemaker se Putte
story: Isak kry nie soveel stories soos sy pa Abraham of sy seun Jakob nie, maar Genesis 26 wys ons iets spesiaals van hom: hy was ’n vredemaker.

God het Isak so baie geseën dat sy oeste honderd keer meer opgelewer het as wat hy geplant het, en sy troppe en kuddes het baie groot geword. Dit het die Filistyne jaloers gemaak. Hulle het sy pa se ou putte met grond toegegooi, en die koning het vir hom gesê om weg te trek.

In daardie droë land was putte meer werd as goud. Toe Isak se diensknegte ’n nuwe put grawe en vars water kry, het die plaaslike veewagters gestry: ‘Die water is ons s’n!’ Isak het dit Esek genoem, wat ‘rusie’ beteken, en aangetrek. Hulle het nog een gegrawe, en die veewagters het weer gestry. Hy het dit Sitna genoem, ‘teenstand’, en weer aangetrek.

Hulle het ’n derde put gegrawe, en hierdie keer het niemand gestry nie. Isak het dit Rehobot genoem, ‘ruimte’, en gesê: ‘Nou het die Here vir ons ruimte gegee en sal ons in die land voorspoedig wees.’

Daardie nag het God aan hom verskyn: ‘Moenie bang wees nie, want Ek is by jou; Ek sal jou seën.’ Isak het ’n altaar gebou en aanbid. Kort daarna het die einste koning wat hom weggestuur het, gekom om ’n vredesverdrag te sluit, en gesê: ‘Ons het duidelik gesien dat die Here by jou is.’

Isak kon vir sy regte baklei het. In plaas daarvan het hy God vertrou om te voorsien. Om vrede te maak het hom nie ’n verloorder gemaak nie; dit het plek gemaak vir God om hom te seën, en selfs sy vyande gewen. As jy vrede kies, vertrou jy dat God groot genoeg is om na jou te kyk.

verse.text: Gelukkig is die wat vrede maak, want hulle sal kinders van God genoem word.

lessons: Vredemakers vertrou God in plaas daarvan om vir alles te baklei.
God maak plek vir sy kinders as hulle Hom vertrou.
’n Vreedsame lewe kan selfs ons teenstanders wen.
questions: Wat beteken die name Esek, Sitna en Rehobot? Hoekom dink jy het Isak hulle gekies?
Hoekom het die koning dalk van plan verander oor Isak?
Waar is ’n situasie waar jy vrede kan kies in plaas van ’n argument?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra God: ‘Is daar ’n argument waarvan U wil hê ek moet wegstap, of vrede wat U wil hê ek moet maak?’ Luister en skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Here, dankie dat U vir my plek maak.
Help my om vrede te maak met…
Ek vertrou U om vir my te sorg.

mission.text: Kies hierdie week, as ’n argument begin, om die eerste een te wees wat dit kalmeer.

af.journal: Teken drie putte en noem hulle Esek, Sitna en Rehobot. Skryf langs elkeen oor ’n tyd in jou lewe wat soos daardie put voel.

en.title: Strength Under Control
story: Genesis 26 tells a quiet story about water and quarrels that turns out to say a lot about strength.

Isaac was not weak. By verse 13 he was ‘very wealthy’; so powerful, in fact, that the Philistine king Abimelek said, ‘You have become too powerful for us.’ Isaac could easily have defended his wells by force. Yet three times, when local herders claimed the water his servants had dug for, he moved on. He named the wells after his experiences: Esek (‘dispute’), Sitnah (‘opposition’), and finally Rehoboth (‘room’), where ‘they did not quarrel’.

Was Isaac a pushover? No. This is what the Bible calls meekness: strength under control. A powerful horse that is gentle in its rider’s hands isn’t weak; it is trained. Isaac had the power to fight, and chose not to, because he trusted God to provide. Jesus said, ‘Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.’ Isaac literally ended up with room in the land.

God confirmed Isaac’s choice that very night: ‘Do not be afraid, for I am with you.’ And notice what peacemaking did to his enemies. Abimelek came with his advisers and said, ‘We saw clearly that the Lord was with you.’ Isaac threw them a feast and made a peace treaty. That same day his servants found water at another well. Peace and provision arrived together.

In a world where people fight hard for their rights, their image and the last word, especially online, Isaac’s story is countercultural. It doesn’t mean you never stand up for what is right. Justice matters, and sometimes we must speak up, especially for others. But it does mean you don’t have to win every argument to be secure. When your security is in God, you can afford to be generous.
Jesus called peacemakers ‘children of God’. They look like their Father, the ultimate Peacemaker, who made peace with us through the cross.

verse.text: Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth… Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.

lessons: Meekness is not weakness; it is strength under control.
When our security is in God, we don’t need to win every argument.
Peacemakers look like their Father, who made peace with us through Jesus.
questions: What is the difference between meekness and weakness?
When should we speak up for what is right, and when should we let something go?
Where do you most often fight for ‘the last word’, at home, at school or online?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Ask God: ‘Is there a conflict where you want me to choose peace?’ Write down what you sense, and one step you could take.
prayer: Father, thank you for making peace with me through Jesus.
Give me strength under control in…
Make me a peacemaker who looks like you.

mission.text: This week, let someone else have the last word in a disagreement that doesn’t really matter, and pray for them instead.

en.journal: Write about an argument you ‘won’ that you now wish you had handled differently. What would meekness have looked like?

af.title: Krag onder Beheer
story: Genesis 26 vertel ’n stil storie oor water en rusies wat baie blyk te sê oor krag.

Isak was nie swak nie. Teen vers 13 was hy ‘baie ryk’; so magtig, inderdaad, dat die Filistynse koning Abimeleg gesê het: ‘Jy het te magtig vir ons geword.’ Isak kon maklik sy putte met geweld verdedig het. Tog het hy drie keer, toe plaaslike veewagters die water opeis waarvoor sy diensknegte gegrawe het, aangetrek. Hy het die putte na sy ervarings genoem: Esek (‘rusie’), Sitna (‘teenstand’), en eindelik Rehobot (‘ruimte’), waar ‘hulle nie gestry het nie’.

Was Isak ’n swakkeling? Nee. Dit is wat die Bybel sagmoedigheid noem: krag onder beheer. ’n Sterk perd wat sag is in sy ruiter se hande, is nie swak nie; dit is geleer. Isak het die krag gehad om te baklei, en het gekies om dit nie te doen nie, omdat hy God vertrou het om te voorsien. Jesus het gesê: ‘Gelukkig is die sagmoediges, want hulle sal die aarde besit.’ Isak het letterlik met ruimte in die land geëindig.

God het Isak se keuse daardie selfde nag bevestig: ‘Moenie bang wees nie, want Ek is by jou.’ En let op wat vrede maak aan sy vyande gedoen het. Abimeleg het met sy raadgewers gekom en gesê: ‘Ons het duidelik gesien dat die Here by jou is.’ Isak het vir hulle ’n fees gehou en ’n vredesverdrag gesluit. Daardie selfde dag het sy diensknegte water by nog ’n put gekry. Vrede en voorsiening het saam aangekom.

In ’n wêreld waar mense hard baklei vir hulle regte, hulle beeld en die laaste woord, veral aanlyn, gaan Isak se storie teen die stroom in. Dit beteken nie jy staan nooit op vir wat reg is nie. Geregtigheid maak saak, en soms moet ons praat, veral vir ander. Maar dit beteken jy hoef nie elke argument te wen om veilig te voel nie. As jou sekuriteit in God is, kan jy bekostig om vrygewig te wees.
Jesus het vredemakers ‘kinders van God’ genoem. Hulle lyk soos hulle Vader, die grootste Vredemaker, wat deur die kruis vrede met ons gemaak het.

verse.text: Gelukkig is die sagmoediges, want hulle sal die aarde besit… Gelukkig is die wat vrede maak, want hulle sal kinders van God genoem word.

lessons: Sagmoedigheid is nie swakheid nie; dit is krag onder beheer.
As ons sekuriteit in God is, hoef ons nie elke argument te wen nie.
Vredemakers lyk soos hulle Vader, wat deur Jesus vrede met ons gemaak het.
questions: Wat is die verskil tussen sagmoedigheid en swakheid?
Wanneer moet ons opstaan vir wat reg is, en wanneer moet ons iets laat gaan?
Waar baklei jy die meeste vir ‘die laaste woord’, by die huis, by die skool of aanlyn?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Vra God: ‘Is daar ’n konflik waar U wil hê ek vrede moet kies?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel, en een tree wat jy kan neem.
prayer: Vader, dankie dat U deur Jesus vrede met my gemaak het.
Gee my krag onder beheer in…
Maak my ’n vredemaker wat soos U lyk.

mission.text: Laat hierdie week iemand anders die laaste woord hê in ’n meningsverskil wat nie regtig saak maak nie, en bid eerder vir hulle.

af.journal: Skryf oor ’n argument wat jy ‘gewen’ het wat jy nou wens jy anders hanteer het. Hoe sou sagmoedigheid gelyk het?

en.title: Isaac Digs a Well

But some men said, ‘That’s OUR well!’ Isaac didn’t fight.
He dug another one. ‘That’s ours too!’ they said.
Isaac moved and dug again. This time nobody argued!
‘God has made room for us!’ said Isaac.

verse.text: Blessed are the peacemakers.

en.action: Dig, dig, dig with your hands! Then give a big thumbs up: ‘God made room!’
lessons: I can be kind instead of fighting.

prayer: Dear God,
help me to be a peacemaker. Amen.

af.title: Isak Grawe ’n Put

Maar ’n paar mans het gesê: ‘Dis ONS put!’ Isak het nie baklei nie.
Hy het nog een gegrawe. ‘Daai een is ook ons s’n!’ het hulle gesê.
Isak het aangetrek en weer gegrawe. Hierdie keer het niemand gestry nie!
‘God het vir ons plek gemaak!’ het Isak gesê.

af.action: Grawe, grawe, grawe met jou hande! Gee dan ’n groot duim op: ‘God het plek gemaak!’

en.title: Room to Grow
story: Isaac lived in a dry land where water was very precious. God blessed Isaac, and his flocks and crops grew and grew. But some of the people around him became jealous.
Isaac’s servants dug a well, and fresh water bubbled up. But the local herdsmen came and argued: ‘That water is ours!’ Isaac could have fought. Instead, he moved away and dug another well.

‘That one’s ours too!’ the herdsmen shouted. Again Isaac didn’t fight. He moved on and dug a third well. This time, nobody argued. Isaac named it Rehoboth, which means ‘room’. ‘Now the Lord has given us room,’ he said.
That night, God spoke to Isaac: ‘Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bless you.’ Later, even the king who had been unkind came to make peace with Isaac.
It isn’t always easy to walk away from an argument. But when we trust God, we don’t have to fight for everything. God makes room for His children.

verse.text: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.

lessons: We can choose peace instead of fighting.
God takes care of us when we trust Him.
God makes room for His children.
questions: What did Isaac do when people argued with him?
When do you feel like fighting? What could you do instead?
prayer: Dear God,
help me to be a peacemaker.
When I want to fight,
help me to trust you instead. Amen.

mission.text: If you start to argue with someone tomorrow, try being the first one to make peace.

en.title: Surely the Lord Is in This Place
story: Jacob had deceived his blind father and stolen the blessing meant for his brother Esau. Esau was so angry that he planned to kill him. So Jacob fled, leaving home with nothing but a staff in his hand.
As the sun set, he stopped in an empty place, put a stone under his head and lay down to sleep. He was alone, guilty and afraid of the future.

Then he dreamed. A stairway stood on the earth, its top reaching heaven, and angels were going up and down on it. Above it stood the Lord, who said: ‘I am the Lord, the God of your father Abraham and the God of Isaac… I am with you and will watch over you wherever you go… I will not leave you until I have done what I have promised you.’

Notice what God didn’t say. He didn’t say, ‘Now that you’ve cheated your family, you’re on your own.’ God came to Jacob at his lowest point with grace, not condemnation. That doesn’t mean what Jacob did was okay; God would deal with Jacob’s character over many years. But God’s first word to the runaway was a promise.
Jacob woke and said, ‘Surely the Lord is in this place, and I was not aware of it.’ He called the place Bethel, ‘house of God’.

Centuries later, Jesus told Nathanael that he would see ‘heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man’. Jesus is the true stairway between heaven and earth. Through Him, God comes close to us, wherever we are.

verse.text: I am with you and will watch over you wherever you go.

lessons: God is present even in lonely, unexpected places.
God meets us with grace, even at our lowest point.
Jesus is the true stairway, connecting heaven and earth.
questions: How do you think Jacob felt before and after his dream?
Why do you think God was kind to Jacob even though he had done wrong?
Where is a place you need to remember ‘Surely the Lord is in this place’?
en.listen: Be still and say, ‘Surely the Lord is in this place.’ Ask God: ‘How are you with me right here?’ Listen and write down what you sense.
prayer: Lord, you are with me wherever I go.
Thank you for meeting me with grace, even when…

af.title: Die Here Is Regtig op Hierdie Plek
story: Jakob het sy blinde pa bedrieg en die seën gesteel wat vir sy broer Esau bedoel was. Esau was so kwaad dat hy beplan het om hom dood te maak. Toe het Jakob gevlug, en die huis verlaat met niks behalwe ’n kierie in sy hand nie.
Toe die son ondergaan, het hy op ’n leë plek stilgehou, ’n klip onder sy kop gesit en gaan lê om te slaap. Hy was alleen, skuldig en bang vir die toekoms.

Toe het hy gedroom. ’n Trap het op die aarde gestaan, met die bopunt tot in die hemel, en engele het daarop op en af gegaan. Bo-aan het die Here gestaan, en gesê: ‘Ek is die Here, die God van jou vader Abraham en die God van Isak… Ek is by jou en Ek sal oor jou waak oral waar jy gaan… Ek sal jou nie verlaat voordat Ek gedoen het wat Ek jou belowe het nie.’

Let op wat God nie gesê het nie. Hy het nie gesê: ‘Nou dat jy jou familie gekul het, is jy op jou eie nie.’ God het na Jakob gekom op sy laagste punt, met genade, nie veroordeling nie. Dit beteken nie wat Jakob gedoen het, was reg nie; God sou oor baie jare met Jakob se karakter werk. Maar God se eerste woord aan die weghardloper was ’n belofte.
Jakob het wakker geword en gesê: ‘Die Here is regtig op hierdie plek, en ek het dit nie geweet nie.’ Hy het die plek Bet-El genoem, ‘huis van God’.

Eeue later het Jesus vir Natanael gesê dat hy ‘die hemel oop sal sien, en die engele van God wat opklim en neerdaal op die Seun van die mens’. Jesus is die ware trap tussen hemel en aarde. Deur Hom kom God naby aan ons, waar ons ook al is.

verse.text: Ek is by jou en Ek sal oor jou waak oral waar jy gaan.

lessons: God is teenwoordig selfs op eensame, onverwagte plekke.
God ontmoet ons met genade, selfs op ons laagste punt.
Jesus is die ware trap wat hemel en aarde verbind.
questions: Hoe dink jy het Jakob voor en ná sy droom gevoel?
Hoekom dink jy was God goed vir Jakob al het hy verkeerd gedoen?
Waar is ’n plek waar jy moet onthou ‘Die Here is regtig op hierdie plek’?
af.listen: Wees stil en sê: ‘Die Here is regtig op hierdie plek.’ Vra God: ‘Hoe is U hier by my?’ Luister en skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Here, U is by my oral waar ek gaan.
Dankie dat U my met genade ontmoet, selfs wanneer…
Dankie dat Jesus die hemel naby bring.

mission.text: Gaan môre staan, oral waar jy gaan, en sê saggies: ‘Die Here is regtig op hierdie plek.’

af.journal: Teken Jakob se trap. Skryf onderaan ’n plek waar jy eensaam of onseker voel. Skryf bo-aan God se belofte uit Genesis 28:15.

en.title: Grace for a Runaway
story: Jacob is one of the most complicated characters in the Bible. He grasped his twin brother’s heel at birth. He bargained Esau out of his birthright for a bowl of stew. Then, with his mother’s help, he dressed up as Esau and lied to his blind father to steal the family blessing. When Esau vowed to kill him, Jacob fled.
So when Jacob lies down alone at Bethel with a stone for a pillow, he is reaping what he has sown: guilt, fear and isolation. This is exactly the moment God chooses to show up.

In his dream Jacob sees a stairway (or ramp) connecting earth and heaven, with angels ascending and descending, and the Lord standing above it. God repeats to Jacob the promises He made to Abraham: land, descendants, and that ‘all peoples on earth will be blessed through you and your offspring’. Then He adds something personal: ‘I am with you and will watch over you wherever you go… I will not leave you.’

This is grace: undeserved favour. Jacob hadn’t repented yet. He hadn’t made things right with Esau. His character still needed years of work (and God would wrestle with him later!). But God’s commitment to him didn’t depend on his performance.
Jacob’s response is honest but a little transactional: ‘If God will be with me… then the Lord will be my God.’ He is still a bargainer! God would patiently grow him from there.

Jesus connected this story to Himself. He told Nathanael: ‘You will see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.’ Jesus is the stairway. Heaven and earth meet in Him. We don’t climb up to God by our goodness; God comes down to us in Jesus.
Whatever you have done, wherever you are running, God’s first word to you through Jesus is not ‘You’re on your own’, but ‘I am with you.’

verse.text: I am with you and will watch over you wherever you go… I will not leave you.

lessons: Grace is God’s undeserved favour; it meets us before we have it all together.
God patiently grows our character over time.
Jesus is the stairway between heaven and earth: God comes down to us in Him.
questions: What had Jacob done to end up alone at Bethel?
Why is it significant that God made His promise before Jacob changed?
How does Jesus’ claim in John 1:51 change the way you read Jacob’s dream?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Picture the stairway with Jesus as the connection between you and heaven. Ask: ‘Lord, what do you want to say to me where I am right now?’ Write it down.
prayer: God, thank you for your grace, which reaches me before I have it all together.
Keep growing my character, especially in…
Thank you that in Jesus, heaven has come close to me.

mission.text: This week, when you feel you have messed up, instead of hiding, pray: ‘Thank you that you are still with me.’

en.journal: Jacob tried to bargain with God (‘If you… then I…’). Write about any ways you try to bargain with God. How is grace different?

af.title: Genade vir ’n Weghardloper
story: Jakob is een van die mees ingewikkelde karakters in die Bybel. Hy het by sy geboorte sy tweelingbroer se hakskeen gegryp. Hy het Esau se eersgeboortereg vir ’n bord bredie afgeding. Toe het hy, met sy ma se hulp, soos Esau aangetrek en vir sy blinde pa gelieg om die familieseën te steel. Toe Esau sweer om hom dood te maak, het Jakob gevlug.
So wanneer Jakob alleen by Bet-El gaan lê met ’n klip as kussing, oes hy wat hy gesaai het: skuld, vrees en isolasie. Dit is presies die oomblik wat God kies om op te daag.

In sy droom sien Jakob ’n trap (of opritbaan) wat aarde en hemel verbind, met engele wat opklim en neerdaal, en die Here wat bo-aan staan. God herhaal vir Jakob die beloftes wat Hy aan Abraham gemaak het: land, nakomelinge, en dat ‘al die volke van die aarde deur jou en jou nageslag geseën sal word’. Dan voeg Hy iets persoonliks by: ‘Ek is by jou en Ek sal oor jou waak oral waar jy gaan… Ek sal jou nie verlaat nie.’

Dit is genade: onverdiende guns. Jakob het hom nog nie bekeer nie. Hy het nog nie dinge met Esau reggemaak nie. Sy karakter het nog jare se werk nodig gehad (en God sou later met hom stoei!). Maar God se toewyding aan hom het nie van sy prestasie afgehang nie.
Jakob se reaksie is eerlik, maar ’n bietjie soos ’n ooreenkoms: ‘As God by my is… dan sal die Here my God wees.’ Hy is nog steeds ’n onderhandelaar! God sou hom van daar af geduldig laat groei.

Jesus het hierdie storie met Homself verbind. Hy het vir Natanael gesê: ‘Julle sal die hemel oop sien, en die engele van God wat opklim en neerdaal op die Seun van die mens.’ Jesus is die trap. Hemel en aarde ontmoet mekaar in Hom. Ons klim nie deur ons goedheid na God op nie; God kom in Jesus na ons af.
Wat jy ook al gedoen het, waarheen jy ook al weghardloop, God se eerste woord aan jou deur Jesus is nie ‘Jy is op jou eie’ nie, maar ‘Ek is by jou.’

verse.text: Ek is by jou en Ek sal oor jou waak oral waar jy gaan… Ek sal jou nie verlaat nie.

lessons: Genade is God se onverdiende guns; dit ontmoet ons voordat ons alles reg het.
God laat ons karakter geduldig oor tyd groei.
Jesus is die trap tussen hemel en aarde: God kom in Hom na ons af.
questions: Wat het Jakob gedoen om alleen by Bet-El te beland?
Hoekom is dit betekenisvol dat God sy belofte gemaak het voordat Jakob verander het?
Hoe verander Jesus se uitspraak in Johannes 1:51 die manier waarop jy Jakob se droom lees?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Stel jou die trap voor met Jesus as die verbinding tussen jou en die hemel. Vra: ‘Here, wat wil U vir my sê waar ek nou is?’ Skryf dit neer.
prayer: God, dankie vir u genade, wat my bereik voordat ek alles reg het.
Laat my karakter aanhou groei, veral in…
Dankie dat die hemel in Jesus naby aan my gekom het.

mission.text: As jy hierdie week voel jy het iets opgemors, bid eerder as om weg te kruip: ‘Dankie dat U steeds by my is.’

af.journal: Jakob het probeer om met God te onderhandel (‘As U… dan sal ek…’). Skryf oor enige maniere waarop jy met God probeer onderhandel. Hoe is genade anders?

en.title: Wrestling with God
story: After twenty years away, Jacob was finally heading home, with his wives, children and flocks. But news came that his brother Esau was coming to meet him with four hundred men. Jacob was terrified.

He did two things. He planned: he sent waves of gifts ahead to soften Esau’s anger. And he prayed one of the most honest prayers in Genesis: ‘I am unworthy of all the kindness and faithfulness you have shown your servant… Save me, I pray, from the hand of my brother Esau, for I am afraid.’

That night, alone by the Jabbok River, a man wrestled with him until daybreak. When the man saw that he couldn’t win, he touched Jacob’s hip so that it was wrenched out of its socket. But Jacob still held on: ‘I will not let you go unless you bless me.’
‘What is your name?’ the man asked. It was a painful question, because ‘Jacob’ was connected with grasping and deceiving. Saying his name was like admitting who he had been.

Then came the blessing: ‘Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with humans and have overcome.’ Jacob realised: ‘I saw God face to face, and yet my life was spared.’ He limped as the sun rose, a changed man.

Sometimes our relationship with God includes wrestling: with hard questions, with our own pride or with things we don’t understand. God isn’t offended by that. Hold on to Him. He uses the struggle to change us, and He gives us a new name.

verse.text: I will not let you go unless you bless me.

lessons: God welcomes honest prayers, even prayers full of fear.
God uses our struggles to change our character.
God gives His children a new identity.
questions: What did Jacob do when he was afraid? What can we learn from his prayer?
Why was it important for Jacob to say his name?
What is something you are ‘wrestling’ with God about right now?
en.listen: Bring God something you are struggling with. Hold on to Him in prayer. Ask: ‘How do you want to bless me through this?’ Listen and write it down.
prayer: God, I won’t let go of you.
I am wrestling with…

mission.text: If something worries you this week, write an honest prayer like Jacob’s: tell God exactly how you feel, and ask Him to help.

en.journal: Write your own honest prayer like Jacob’s in Genesis 32:9–12: admit your fear, thank God for His kindness, and ask for His help.

af.title: Stoei met God
story: Ná twintig jaar weg was Jakob eindelik op pad huis toe, met sy vroue, kinders en troppe. Maar nuus het gekom dat sy broer Esau hom met vierhonderd mans tegemoet kom. Jakob was doodbang.

Hy het twee dinge gedoen. Hy het beplan: hy het golwe geskenke vooruit gestuur om Esau se woede te versag. En hy het een van die eerlikste gebede in Genesis gebid: ‘Ek is nie werd al die goedheid en trou wat U aan u dienaar bewys het nie… Red my tog uit die hand van my broer Esau, want ek is bang.’

Daardie nag, alleen by die Jabbokrivier, het ’n man met hom gestoei tot dagbreek. Toe die man sien hy kan nie wen nie, het hy aan Jakob se heup geraak sodat dit uit lit geruk is. Maar Jakob het steeds vasgehou: ‘Ek sal jou nie laat gaan voordat jy my seën nie.’
‘Wat is jou naam?’ het die man gevra. Dit was ’n pynlike vraag, want ‘Jakob’ was verbind met gryp en bedrieg. Om sy naam te sê, was soos om te erken wie hy was.

Toe kom die seën: ‘Jou naam sal nie meer Jakob wees nie, maar Israel, want jy het met God en met mense gestoei en jy het oorwin.’ Jakob het besef: ‘Ek het God van aangesig tot aangesig gesien, en tog het ek bly lewe.’ Hy het mank geloop toe die son opkom, ’n veranderde man.

Soms sluit ons verhouding met God stoei in: met moeilike vrae, met ons eie trots of met dinge wat ons nie verstaan nie. God is nie daardeur beledig nie. Hou aan Hom vas. Hy gebruik die stryd om ons te verander, en Hy gee ons ’n nuwe naam.

verse.text: Ek sal jou nie laat gaan voordat jy my seën nie.

lessons: God verwelkom eerlike gebede, selfs gebede vol vrees.
God gebruik ons stryd om ons karakter te verander.
God gee sy kinders ’n nuwe identiteit.
questions: Wat het Jakob gedoen toe hy bang was? Wat kan ons uit sy gebed leer?
Hoekom was dit belangrik vir Jakob om sy naam te sê?
Waaroor ‘stoei’ jy nou met God?
af.listen: Bring vir God iets waarmee jy sukkel. Hou in gebed aan Hom vas. Vra: ‘Hoe wil U my hierdeur seën?’ Luister en skryf dit neer.
prayer: God, ek sal U nie los nie.
Ek stoei met…
Dankie dat U my ’n nuwe naam as u kind gee.

mission.text: As iets jou hierdie week bekommer, skryf ’n eerlike gebed soos Jakob s’n: vertel God presies hoe jy voel, en vra Hom om te help.

af.journal: Skryf jou eie eerlike gebed soos Jakob s’n in Genesis 32:9–12: erken jou vrees, dank God vir sy goedheid, en vra vir sy hulp.

en.title: The Limp and the Name
story: Genesis 32 is one of the strangest and most profound chapters in the Bible. Jacob, the lifelong schemer, is about to meet the brother he cheated. Esau is coming with four hundred men, and Jacob assumes the worst.

First, notice Jacob’s prayer in verses 9–12. It is the first time we hear him pray with real humility: ‘I am unworthy of all the kindness and faithfulness you have shown your servant.’ Then he is completely honest: ‘I am afraid.’ Fear brought Jacob to his knees, and that’s often where God begins His deepest work in us.

Then, alone at night by the river, ‘a man wrestled with him till daybreak’. The text gradually reveals who this is: Jacob later says, ‘I saw God face to face.’ The prophet Hosea calls him an angel. Many Christians have seen here a pre-incarnate appearance of God the Son.

Think about the symbolism. Jacob has wrestled with people all his life, grasping for blessings, outmanoeuvring his brother and his uncle. Now he wrestles with God Himself, and he cannot win by tricks. God touches his hip, and Jacob is injured. Yet he clings on: ‘I will not let you go unless you bless me.’ He has finally realised that the blessing he needs can’t be stolen; it must be received from God.
Before blessing him, God asks: ‘What is your name?’ To say ‘Jacob’ is to confess ‘deceiver’. Real change starts with honest confession. Then God gives him a new name, Israel, and a new identity.
Jacob walks away limping. That limp is important. God’s deepest blessings often come through weakness, not around it. Paul later wrote that God told him, ‘My power is made perfect in weakness.’
If you are wrestling with God, with questions, with sin or with pain, don’t let go. The struggle may leave a limp, but it can also bring a new name.

verse.text: My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.

lessons: Fear and honesty often bring us to the place where God does His deepest work.
Real change begins with honest confession of who we have been.
God’s blessings often come through our weakness, not around it.
questions: What is different about Jacob’s prayer in verses 9–12 compared to his earlier bargaining at Bethel?
Why do you think God asked Jacob his name?
What weakness or ‘limp’ in your life might God want to use?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Tell God honestly what you are wrestling with. Then ask: ‘What new name do you want to give me?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: God, I am unworthy of your kindness, and I am honest about my fear of…
I won’t let go until you bless me.
Thank you that your power is made perfect in my weakness.

mission.text: Write your own Genesis 32:9–12 prayer this week: humble, honest and specific.

en.journal: Write your old ‘name’ (a word that describes who you have sometimes been) and the new name God gives you in Christ. What changes when you live from the new one?

af.title: Die Mank Been en die Naam
story: Genesis 32 is een van die vreemdste en diepste hoofstukke in die Bybel. Jakob, die lewenslange planmaker, staan op die punt om die broer te ontmoet wat hy bedrieg het. Esau kom met vierhonderd mans, en Jakob verwag die ergste.

Let eers op Jakob se gebed in verse 9–12. Dit is die eerste keer dat ons hom met ware nederigheid hoor bid: ‘Ek is nie werd al die goedheid en trou wat U aan u dienaar bewys het nie.’ Dan is hy heeltemal eerlik: ‘Ek is bang.’ Vrees het Jakob op sy knieë gebring, en dit is dikwels waar God sy diepste werk in ons begin.

Dan, alleen in die nag by die rivier, ‘het ’n man met hom gestoei tot dagbreek’. Die teks wys geleidelik wie dit is: Jakob sê later: ‘Ek het God van aangesig tot aangesig gesien.’ Die profeet Hosea noem hom ’n engel. Baie Christene het hier ’n verskyning van God die Seun gesien voordat Hy mens geword het.

Dink aan die simboliek. Jakob het sy hele lewe lank met mense gestoei, na seëninge gegryp, sy broer en sy oom uitoorlê. Nou stoei hy met God self, en hy kan nie met truuks wen nie. God raak aan sy heup, en Jakob word beseer. Tog klou hy vas: ‘Ek sal jou nie laat gaan voordat jy my seën nie.’ Hy het eindelik besef dat die seën wat hy nodig het, nie gesteel kan word nie; dit moet van God ontvang word.
Voordat Hy hom seën, vra God: ‘Wat is jou naam?’ Om ‘Jakob’ te sê, is om ‘bedrieër’ te bely. Ware verandering begin met eerlike belydenis. Dan gee God hom ’n nuwe naam, Israel, en ’n nuwe identiteit.

Jakob stap mank weg. Daardie mank been is belangrik. God se diepste seëninge kom dikwels deur swakheid, nie om dit nie. Paulus het later geskryf dat God vir hom gesê het: ‘My krag kom juis tot volle werking wanneer jy swak is.’
As jy met God stoei, met vrae, met sonde of met pyn, moenie los nie. Die stryd laat jou dalk mank, maar dit kan ook ’n nuwe naam bring.

verse.text: My genade is vir jou genoeg, want my krag kom juis tot volle werking wanneer jy swak is.

lessons: Vrees en eerlikheid bring ons dikwels na die plek waar God sy diepste werk doen.
Ware verandering begin met eerlike belydenis van wie ons was.
God se seëninge kom dikwels deur ons swakheid, nie om dit nie.
questions: Wat is anders aan Jakob se gebed in verse 9–12 as sy vroeëre onderhandeling by Bet-El?
Hoekom dink jy het God Jakob sy naam gevra?
Watter swakheid of ‘mank been’ in jou lewe wil God dalk gebruik?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Vertel God eerlik waarmee jy stoei. Vra dan: ‘Watter nuwe naam wil U my gee?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, ek is u goedheid nie werd nie, en ek is eerlik oor my vrees vir…
Ek sal nie los voordat U my seën nie.
Dankie dat u krag in my swakheid tot volle werking kom.

mission.text: Skryf hierdie week jou eie Genesis 32:9–12-gebed: nederig, eerlik en spesifiek.

af.journal: Skryf jou ou ‘naam’ (’n woord wat beskryf wie jy soms was) en die nuwe naam wat God jou in Christus gee. Wat verander as jy uit die nuwe een lewe?

en.title: Jacob Gets a New Name
story: One night, Jacob wrestled with a mysterious man. Push, pull!
They wrestled all night long, until the sun came up.
Jacob said, ‘Please bless me!’
God gave him a brand-new name: Israel!
God gives me a new name too: child of God!

verse.text: You are God’s child.

en.action: Give Mom a gentle wrestle-hug: push, pull! Then say: ‘My name is child of God!’
lessons: God calls me His child.
questions: What is your name? And what does God call you? (His child!)
prayer: Thank you, God,
that I am your child. Amen.

af.title: Jakob Kry ’n Nuwe Naam
story: Een nag het Jakob met ’n geheimsinnige man gestoei. Druk, trek!
Hulle het die hele nag gestoei, totdat die son opgekom het.
Jakob het gesê: ‘Seën my asseblief!’
God het hom ’n splinternuwe naam gegee: Israel!
God gee my ook ’n nuwe naam: kind van God!

verse.text: Jy is God se kind.

af.action: Gee vir Mamma ’n sagte stoei-drukkie: druk, trek! Sê dan: ‘My naam is kind van God!’
lessons: God noem my sy kind.
questions: Wat is jou naam? En wat noem God jou? (Sy kind!)
prayer: Dankie, God,
dat ek u kind is. Amen.

en.title: A Brand-New Name
story: Twenty years after running away, Jacob was going home. But he was afraid, because he would have to meet his brother Esau, the brother he had tricked.

The night before, Jacob was alone by a river. Suddenly a mysterious man grabbed him, and they wrestled all night long! As the sun began to rise, the man touched Jacob’s hip, and it hurt. But Jacob held on tight. ‘I won’t let you go unless you bless me!’
The man asked, ‘What is your name?’ ‘Jacob,’ he answered. The name Jacob means something like ‘tricker’. Jacob had to admit who he had been.

Then the man said, ‘Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with people and have overcome.’ Jacob realised he had been wrestling with God Himself! He limped away that morning, but he was a changed man with a new name.
God still gives new names. When we belong to Jesus, God doesn’t call us by our old mistakes. He calls us His children, loved and new.

verse.text: See what great love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God!

lessons: God can change who we are.
We can be honest with God about our mistakes.
God gives us a new name: His children.
questions: Why do you think Jacob held on so tightly?
What new name does God give everyone who belongs to Jesus?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you change me
and give me a new name.
I am your child. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, if you feel bad about a mistake, say: ‘God calls me His child, not my mistake.’

en.title: Running to Forgive
story: The sun was up, Jacob was limping, and there on the horizon was Esau with four hundred men. Jacob arranged his family behind him and went ahead, bowing to the ground seven times as he approached his brother. In that culture, it was how a servant approached a king. Jacob, who had once grabbed the blessing, was now humbling himself.

Then the unexpected happened. ‘Esau ran to meet Jacob and embraced him; he threw his arms around his neck and kissed him. And they wept.’ The brother who had been wronged, who had every reason for revenge, ran to forgive.

Does that remind you of another story? Jesus told of a father who saw his runaway son from a long way off, ‘ran to his son, threw his arms around him and kissed him’. The words are almost exactly the same! Jesus may have had Esau in mind. Forgiveness that runs is a picture of God’s own heart.

Jacob insisted that Esau keep the gifts and said something remarkable: ‘To see your face is like seeing the face of God, now that you have received me favourably.’ When we experience forgiveness, we catch a glimpse of what God is like.

Forgiveness doesn’t pretend that what happened didn’t matter. Esau had been badly hurt. But he chose not to hold it over his brother any longer. And God had been at work in both brothers’ hearts during those twenty years.
Is there someone you need to forgive, or someone you need to ask for forgiveness? With God’s help, it is possible.

verse.text: Be kind and compassionate to one another, forgiving each other, just as in Christ God forgave you.

lessons: Forgiveness that runs towards others is a picture of God’s heart.
Humility and saying sorry open the door to peace.
God works in hearts over time to make reconciliation possible.
questions: How did Jacob approach Esau? What did that show?
What is similar between Esau and the father in Jesus’ story of the lost son?
Is there someone you need to forgive, or to ask forgiveness from?
en.listen: Be still and ask God: ‘Is there someone you want me to forgive, or say sorry to?’ Listen. Then ask Him for the strength to do it.
prayer: Father, thank you for running to forgive me.
Help me to forgive… / to say sorry to…
Make me someone who makes peace.

mission.text: Take one step this week towards making peace with someone: a message, an apology or a kind act.

en.journal: Compare Genesis 33:4 with Luke 15:20. Write what both verses teach you about forgiveness.

af.title: Hardloop om te Vergewe
story: Die son was op, Jakob het mank geloop, en daar op die horison was Esau met vierhonderd mans. Jakob het sy familie agter hom gerangskik en vooruit gegaan, en sewe keer tot op die grond gebuig terwyl hy nader aan sy broer kom. In daardie kultuur het ’n dienskneg so na ’n koning toe gegaan. Jakob, wat eens die seën gegryp het, het homself nou verneder.

Toe het die onverwagte gebeur. ‘Esau het Jakob tegemoet gehardloop en hom omhels; hy het sy arms om sy nek gegooi en hom gesoen. En hulle het gehuil.’ Die broer wat verontreg is, wat elke rede vir wraak gehad het, het gehardloop om te vergewe.

Herinner dit jou aan ’n ander storie? Jesus het vertel van ’n vader wat sy weggeloopte seun van ver af gesien het, ‘na sy seun toe gehardloop het, sy arms om hom gegooi en hom gesoen het’. Die woorde is amper presies dieselfde! Jesus het dalk aan Esau gedink. Vergifnis wat hardloop, is ’n prentjie van God se eie hart.

Jakob het daarop aangedring dat Esau die geskenke hou, en iets merkwaardigs gesê: ‘Om jou gesig te sien, is soos om die gesig van God te sien, noudat jy my so goed ontvang het.’ As ons vergifnis ervaar, kry ons ’n kykie in hoe God is.

Vergifnis maak nie of wat gebeur het nie saak gemaak het nie. Esau is erg seergemaak. Maar hy het gekies om dit nie langer teen sy broer te hou nie. En God was in daardie twintig jaar in albei broers se harte aan die werk.
Is daar iemand wat jy moet vergewe, of iemand wat jy om vergifnis moet vra? Met God se hulp is dit moontlik.

verse.text: Wees goed en vol deernis teenoor mekaar, en vergewe mekaar soos God julle in Christus vergewe het.

lessons: Vergifnis wat na ander toe hardloop, is ’n prentjie van God se hart.
Nederigheid en jammer sê maak die deur oop vir vrede.
God werk oor tyd in harte om versoening moontlik te maak.
questions: Hoe het Jakob na Esau toe gegaan? Wat het dit gewys?
Wat is soortgelyk tussen Esau en die vader in Jesus se storie van die verlore seun?
Is daar iemand wat jy moet vergewe, of iemand vir wie jy om vergifnis moet vra?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra God: ‘Is daar iemand wat U wil hê ek moet vergewe, of vir wie ek jammer moet sê?’ Luister. Vra Hom dan vir die krag om dit te doen.
prayer: Vader, dankie dat U gehardloop het om my te vergewe.
Help my om… te vergewe / om vir… jammer te sê.
Maak my iemand wat vrede maak.

mission.text: Neem hierdie week een tree om vrede met iemand te maak: ’n boodskap, ’n verskoning of ’n gawe daad.

af.journal: Vergelyk Genesis 33:4 met Lukas 15:20. Skryf wat albei verse jou oor vergifnis leer.

en.title: The Face of God in a Brother
story: After twenty years, a night of wrestling and a new name, Jacob meets Esau. The scene is carefully written, and it rewards slow reading.

Jacob goes ahead of his family and ‘bowed down to the ground seven times as he approached his brother’. This is a deliberate reversal. Years earlier, Jacob had stolen a blessing that said, ‘May your mother’s sons bow down to you.’ Now Jacob bows to Esau. Repentance often looks like undoing, as far as we can, the damage our pride has caused.

Then: ‘Esau ran to meet Jacob and embraced him; he threw his arms around his neck and kissed him. And they wept.’ Read Luke 15:20, the father welcoming the prodigal: ‘He ran to his son, threw his arms around him and kissed him.’ The parallel is striking. In Jesus’ story, the running, embracing figure represents God the Father.

Jacob then says something theologically rich: ‘To see your face is like seeing the face of God, now that you have received me favourably.’ He had just seen God face to face at the river. Now, in his brother’s undeserved welcome, he sees God’s character again. Grace given by people reflects the grace of God.

But the story is also realistic. The brothers reconcile, yet they don’t move in together. Jacob politely declines to travel with Esau and settles elsewhere. Forgiveness and reconciliation are real, but restoring trust and closeness can take time, and sometimes healthy boundaries remain. That is not failure. It is wisdom.

What does this mean for you? First, you can receive God’s forgiveness as freely as Jacob received Esau’s welcome. Second, when you forgive someone, you show them the face of God. Third, forgiveness is a choice you can make even when the relationship needs time to heal.
Is there a brother, sister, friend or classmate you are still holding something against? You may be the one God wants to use to show them His face.

verse.text: To see your face is like seeing the face of God, now that you have received me favourably.

lessons: Repentance often involves humbly undoing the damage our pride has caused.
When we forgive, we reflect the face of God to others.
Forgiveness is a choice; rebuilding trust and closeness can take time.
questions: How does Jacob bowing to Esau reverse the blessing he stole?
Why do you think Jacob said Esau’s welcome was like seeing the face of God?
What is the difference between forgiving someone and fully trusting them again?

af.title: God se Gesig in ’n Broer
story: Ná twintig jaar, ’n nag van stoei en ’n nuwe naam ontmoet Jakob vir Esau. Die toneel is versigtig geskryf, en dit beloon stadige lees.

Jakob gaan voor sy familie uit en ‘het sewe keer tot op die grond gebuig terwyl hy nader aan sy broer kom’. Dit is ’n doelbewuste omkering. Jare vroeër het Jakob ’n seën gesteel wat gesê het: ‘Mag jou moeder se seuns voor jou buig.’ Nou buig Jakob voor Esau. Bekering lyk dikwels daarna om, so ver as wat ons kan, die skade ongedaan te maak wat ons trots veroorsaak het.

Toe: ‘Esau het Jakob tegemoet gehardloop en hom omhels; hy het sy arms om sy nek gegooi en hom gesoen. En hulle het gehuil.’ Lees Lukas 15:20, die vader wat die verlore seun verwelkom: ‘Hy het na sy seun toe gehardloop, sy arms om hom gegooi en hom gesoen.’ Die ooreenkoms is opvallend. In Jesus se storie verteenwoordig die figuur wat hardloop en omhels, God die Vader.

Jakob sê dan iets wat ryk aan teologie is: ‘Om jou gesig te sien, is soos om die gesig van God te sien, noudat jy my so goed ontvang het.’ Hy het pas by die rivier God van aangesig tot aangesig gesien. Nou, in sy broer se onverdiende welkom, sien hy weer God se karakter. Genade wat deur mense gegee word, weerspieël die genade van God.

Maar die storie is ook realisties. Die broers versoen, maar hulle trek nie saam in nie. Jakob weier beleefd om saam met Esau te reis en vestig hom elders. Vergifnis en versoening is werklik, maar om vertroue en nabyheid te herstel kan tyd neem, en soms bly gesonde grense oor. Dit is nie mislukking nie. Dit is wysheid.

Wat beteken dit vir jou? Eerstens kan jy God se vergifnis net so vrylik ontvang as wat Jakob Esau se welkom ontvang het. Tweedens, as jy iemand vergewe, wys jy vir hulle die gesig van God. Derdens is vergifnis ’n keuse wat jy kan maak selfs as die verhouding tyd nodig het om te genees.
Is daar ’n broer, suster, maat of klasmaat teen wie jy nog iets hou? Jy is dalk die een wat God wil gebruik om vir hulle sy gesig te wys.

verse.text: Om jou gesig te sien, is soos om die gesig van God te sien, noudat jy my so goed ontvang het.

lessons: Bekering sluit dikwels in om nederig die skade ongedaan te maak wat ons trots veroorsaak het.

God help ons om vrede te maak.

verse.text: Wees goed vir mekaar en vergewe mekaar.

prayer: Liewe God,

en.title: The Hug Nobody Expected
story: The morning after he wrestled with God, Jacob looked up and saw his brother Esau coming, with four hundred men! Jacob was terrified. Was Esau still angry? Would he want to hurt him?

Jacob had sent gifts ahead: goats, sheep, camels and cows, hoping to make Esau happy. Then he walked towards his brother, bowing down to the ground seven times. He was saying sorry with his whole body.

But Esau didn’t want gifts or bowing. ‘Esau ran to meet Jacob and embraced him; he threw his arms around his neck and kissed him. And they wept.’ The brother who had every reason to be angry chose to forgive!
Jacob said, ‘To see your face is like seeing the face of God.’ Forgiveness is beautiful, because it looks like God. God is the greatest forgiver of all.
Is there someone you have hurt, or someone who has hurt you? With God’s help, enemies can become friends again. Saying sorry and forgiving can turn a scary day into one of the happiest days of all.

verse.text: Be kind and compassionate to one another, forgiving each other, just as in Christ God forgave you.

lessons: Saying sorry and forgiving make peace.
Forgiveness looks like God, because God forgives us.
With God’s help, broken friendships can be made new.
questions: What did Jacob expect Esau to do? What did Esau do?
Is there someone you need to say sorry to, or forgive?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you forgive me.
Help me to say sorry
and to forgive others. Amen.

mission.text: Say sorry to someone tomorrow, or forgive someone, and give them a hug.

af.title: Die Drukkie wat Niemand Verwag Het Nie
story: Die oggend nadat hy met God gestoei het, het Jakob opgekyk en sy broer Esau sien aankom, met vierhonderd mans! Jakob was doodbang. Was Esau nog kwaad? Sou hy hom wou seermaak?

Jakob het geskenke vooruit gestuur: bokke, skape, kamele en koeie, in die hoop om Esau bly te maak. Toe het hy na sy broer toe gestap, en sewe keer tot op die grond gebuig. Hy het met sy hele lyf jammer gesê.

Maar Esau wou nie geskenke of buig hê nie. ‘Esau het hom tegemoet gehardloop en hom omhels; hy het sy arms om sy nek gegooi en hom gesoen. En hulle het gehuil.’ Die broer wat elke rede gehad het om kwaad te wees, het gekies om te vergewe!
Jakob het gesê: ‘Om jou gesig te sien, is soos om die gesig van God te sien.’ Vergifnis is pragtig, want dit lyk soos God. God is die grootste vergewer van almal.

Is daar iemand wat jy seergemaak het, of iemand wat jou seergemaak het? Met God se hulp kan vyande weer vriende word. Om jammer te sê en te vergewe, kan ’n bang dag in een van die gelukkigste dae van almal verander.

verse.text: Wees goed en vol deernis teenoor mekaar, en vergewe mekaar soos God julle in Christus vergewe het.

lessons: Om jammer te sê en te vergewe maak vrede.
Vergifnis lyk soos God, want God vergewe ons.
Met God se hulp kan gebreekte vriendskappe nuut gemaak word.
questions: Wat het Jakob verwag Esau sou doen? Wat het Esau gedoen?
Is daar iemand vir wie jy jammer moet sê, of wat jy moet vergewe?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U my vergewe.
Help my om jammer te sê
en ander te vergewe. Amen.

mission.text: Sê môre vir iemand jammer, of vergewe iemand, en gee hulle ’n drukkie.

en.title: Deborah: Courage That Listens
story: For twenty years, God’s people had been oppressed by Jabin, a Canaanite king. His army commander, Sisera, had nine hundred iron chariots, the most frightening weapon of the time. Israel had no chariots at all.

In those days Deborah was leading Israel. She was a prophet, someone who heard from God and passed on His messages, and she held court under a palm tree between Ramah and Bethel. People came to her to settle their disagreements.
God gave Deborah a message for a man named Barak: ‘Go, take ten thousand men to Mount Tabor. I will lead Sisera to the Kishon River and give him into your hands.’

Barak’s reply showed his fear: ‘If you go with me, I will go; but if you don’t go with me, I won’t go.’ Deborah agreed to go, but she told him that because of his hesitation, the honour of the victory would go to a woman.

On the day of battle Deborah said, ‘Go! This is the day the Lord has given Sisera into your hands. Has not the Lord gone ahead of you?’ Barak charged down the mountain. Judges 5 tells us that heaven itself fought: a storm came and the Kishon River flooded, turning the plain into mud. Those mighty iron chariots were useless!

Deborah’s courage didn’t come from being fearless. It came from listening to God and believing what He said. When you know God is going ahead of you, you can step forward even when the odds look impossible.
Afterwards Deborah and Barak sang a song of praise, giving God all the credit.

verse.text: Be strong and courageous… for the Lord your God will be with you wherever you go.

lessons: Real courage comes from listening to God and believing Him.
God goes ahead of us into battles that look impossible.
When God gives the victory, we give Him the praise.

af.title: Debora: Moed wat Luister
story: Twintig jaar lank is God se mense deur Jabin, ’n Kanaänitiese koning, onderdruk. Sy leërbevelhebber, Sisera, het negehonderd ysterwaens gehad, die vreesaanjaendste wapen van daardie tyd. Israel het glad nie strydwaens gehad nie.

In daardie dae het Debora Israel gelei. Sy was ’n profetes, iemand wat van God gehoor en sy boodskappe oorgedra het, en sy het hof gehou onder ’n palmboom tussen Rama en Bet-El. Mense het na haar gekom om hulle meningsverskille te besleg.
God het vir Debora ’n boodskap gegee vir ’n man met die naam Barak: ‘Gaan, neem tienduisend mans na die berg Tabor. Ek sal Sisera na die Kisonrivier lei en hom in jou hand gee.’

Barak se antwoord het sy vrees gewys: ‘As jy saam met my gaan, sal ek gaan; maar as jy nie saam met my gaan nie, gaan ek nie.’ Debora het ingestem om te gaan, maar sy het vir hom gesê dat die eer van die oorwinning, oor sy huiwering, na ’n vrou sou gaan.

Op die dag van die geveg het Debora gesê: ‘Gaan! Dit is die dag wat die Here Sisera in jou hand gegee het. Het die Here nie voor jou uit gegaan nie?’ Barak het teen die berg afgestorm. Rigters 5 vertel ons dat die hemel self geveg het: ’n storm het gekom en die Kisonrivier het oorgestroom, en die vlakte in modder verander. Daardie magtige ysterwaens was nutteloos!

Debora se moed het nie daarvandaan gekom dat sy nooit bang was nie. Dit het gekom deur na God te luister en te glo wat Hy sê. As jy weet God gaan voor jou uit, kan jy vorentoe tree selfs as die kanse onmoontlik lyk.
Daarna het Debora en Barak ’n loflied gesing, en God al die eer gegee.

verse.text: Wees sterk en dapper… want die Here jou God sal by jou wees oral waar jy gaan.

lessons: Ware moed kom deur na God te luister en Hom te glo.
God gaan voor ons uit in gevegte wat onmoontlik lyk.
As God die oorwinning gee, gee ons Hom die lof.
questions: Hoekom dink jy wou Barak hê Debora moet saam met hom kom?
Hoe het God die ysterwaens hanteer?
Watter ‘ysterwa’ (iets wat vir jou te sterk voel) staan jy voor?

prayer: Here, dankie dat U voor my uit gaan.
Ek is bang vir…
