en.title: A Leader Under a Palm Tree
story: The book of Judges follows a sad cycle: God’s people turn away from Him, they are oppressed by enemies, they cry out to God, and God raises up a deliverer. In Judges 4 the cycle has reached its twentieth year of oppression under Jabin and his commander Sisera, whose nine hundred iron chariots made him seem unbeatable.

Into this situation God speaks through Deborah. She is described as a prophet and as ‘leading Israel’, and she is the only judge in the book who is also called a prophet. People come to her under her palm tree for wise decisions. What made her a leader was not her own strength but her closeness to God: she heard what He said and passed it on faithfully.

Deborah summons Barak with God’s command: gather ten thousand men, and ‘I will give Sisera into your hands’. Barak hesitates: ‘If you go with me, I will go.’ It isn’t entirely wrong to want a godly person beside you, but Barak trusts Deborah’s presence more than God’s promise. So Deborah tells him the honour will go to a woman. That woman turns out to be Jael, who defeats Sisera in her tent.

Deborah’s battle cry is worth memorising: ‘Go! Has not the Lord gone ahead of you?’ The song in chapter 5 fills in the details: ‘The earth shook, the heavens poured… the river Kishon swept them away.’ God sent a storm, and the plain turned to mud. Israel’s greatest fear became completely useless.

There are a few things to notice. First, God uses whoever is willing and listening, man or woman, young or old. Second, courage is not the absence of fear; it is trusting God’s word more than your fear. Third, notice how the story ends: in worship. Deborah and Barak don’t sing about their own bravery. They sing about the Lord.
What is your ‘iron chariot’? Maybe it is a fear, a situation at school or something in your family that feels unbeatable. The God who went ahead of Barak goes ahead of you.

verse.text: Go! This is the day the Lord has given… Has not the Lord gone ahead of you?

lessons: God uses people who are willing and listening, whoever they are.
Courage means trusting God’s word more than our fear.
God’s victories should end in worship, not self-praise.
questions: What made Deborah a good leader?
What was the problem with Barak’s ‘If you go with me…’?
What feels like an ‘iron chariot’ in your life right now?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Picture God going ahead of you into tomorrow. Ask: ‘Lord, what do you want me to know about what I am facing?’ Write it down.
prayer: Lord, thank you that you go ahead of me.
I bring you my ‘iron chariot’: …
Help me trust your word more than my fear.

mission.text: This week, write Judges 4:14 somewhere you will see it before a challenge (a test, a game, a hard conversation).

en.journal: Write your own short ‘Song of Deborah’: a few lines thanking God for a time He went ahead of you.

af.title: ’n Leier onder ’n Palmboom
story: Die boek Rigters volg ’n hartseer kringloop: God se mense draai van Hom af weg, hulle word deur vyande onderdruk, hulle roep na God, en God laat ’n verlosser opstaan. In Rigters 4 het die kringloop sy twintigste jaar van onderdrukking bereik onder Jabin en sy bevelhebber Sisera, wie se negehonderd ysterwaens hom onoorwinlik laat lyk het.

In hierdie situasie praat God deur Debora. Sy word beskryf as ’n profetes en as iemand wat ‘Israel gelei het’, en sy is die enigste rigter in die boek wat ook ’n profetes genoem word. Mense kom na haar onder haar palmboom vir wyse besluite. Wat haar ’n leier gemaak het, was nie haar eie krag nie, maar haar nabyheid aan God: sy het gehoor wat Hy sê en dit getrou oorgedra.

Debora roep Barak met God se bevel: maak tienduisend mans bymekaar, en ‘Ek sal Sisera in jou hand gee’. Barak huiwer: ‘As jy saam met my gaan, sal ek gaan.’ Dit is nie heeltemal verkeerd om ’n gelowige persoon langs jou te wil hê nie, maar Barak vertrou Debora se teenwoordigheid meer as God se belofte. Toe sê Debora vir hom die eer sal na ’n vrou gaan. Daardie vrou blyk Jael te wees, wat Sisera in haar tent oorwin.

Debora se strydkreet is die moeite werd om te memoriseer: ‘Gaan! Het die Here nie voor jou uit gegaan nie?’ Die lied in hoofstuk 5 vul die besonderhede in: ‘Die aarde het gebewe, die hemel het gegiet… die Kisonrivier het hulle weggespoel.’ God het ’n storm gestuur, en die vlakte het in modder verander. Israel se grootste vrees het heeltemal nutteloos geword.

Daar is ’n paar dinge om op te let. Eerstens gebruik God enigiemand wat gewillig is en luister, man of vrou, jonk of oud. Tweedens is moed nie die afwesigheid van vrees nie; dit is om God se woord meer te vertrou as jou vrees. Derdens, let op hoe die storie eindig: in aanbidding. Debora en Barak sing nie oor hulle eie dapperheid nie. Hulle sing oor die Here.
Wat is jou ‘ysterwa’? Dalk is dit ’n vrees, ’n situasie by die skool of iets in jou familie wat onoorwinlik voel. Die God wat voor Barak uit gegaan het, gaan voor jou uit.

verse.text: Gaan! Dit is die dag wat die Here gegee het… Het die Here nie voor jou uit gegaan nie?

lessons: God gebruik mense wat gewillig is en luister, wie hulle ook al is.
Moed beteken om God se woord meer te vertrou as ons vrees.
God se oorwinnings moet in aanbidding eindig, nie in selflof nie.
questions: Wat het Debora ’n goeie leier gemaak?
Wat was die probleem met Barak se ‘As jy saam met my gaan…’?
Wat voel nou soos ’n ‘ysterwa’ in jou lewe?

prayer: Here, dankie dat U voor my uit gaan.

Help my om u woord meer te vertrou as my vrees.

prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you make me brave. Amen.

Being brave doesn’t mean you never feel scared. It means you trust that God is going ahead of you.

God goes ahead of me into hard things.

en.title: The Hero in Hiding
story: For seven years the Midianites had invaded Israel at harvest time. They came with so many camels that they couldn’t be counted, and they ate or took everything. God’s people hid in caves in the mountains.

Gideon was threshing wheat in a winepress. Normally you threshed wheat on a windy hilltop so the wind could blow away the husks. Gideon was doing it down in a pit to hide from the Midianites. That is when the angel of the Lord appeared: ‘The Lord is with you, mighty warrior.’

Gideon didn’t feel like a mighty warrior. He answered with questions and complaints: ‘If the Lord is with us, why has all this happened?… My clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my family.’
God didn’t argue. He simply said, ‘Go in the strength you have… Am I not sending you? I will be with you.’

Gideon still wasn’t sure. He asked for signs, and God patiently gave them. One night Gideon put out a fleece of wool and asked God to make it wet with dew while the ground stayed dry. God did it. Then Gideon asked for the opposite, and God did that too.

Notice that God called Gideon a ‘mighty warrior’ before he had done anything brave. God sees not only who we are now, but who we can become with Him. Our courage doesn’t come from being the strongest or the most important. It comes from God’s promise: ‘I will be with you.’

verse.text: The Lord is with you, mighty warrior… Go in the strength you have.

lessons: God sees who we can become with Him, not only who we are now.
God is patient with our doubts and questions.
Our courage comes from God’s promise to be with us.
questions: Why was Gideon threshing wheat in a winepress?
How did Gideon describe himself? How did God describe him?
What do you think God calls you, even when you don’t feel it?
en.listen: Be still and ask God: ‘What name do you call me?’ Listen for a word like brave, loved, chosen or strong. Write it down.
prayer: Lord, thank you that you see who I can become.
Sometimes I feel like Gideon, especially when…
Help me to go in the strength I have, because you are with me.

mission.text: This week, when you think ‘I can’t’, remind yourself: ‘The Lord is with me. I can go in the strength I have.’

en.journal: Write two lists: ‘What I say about myself’ and ‘What God says about me’. Which list will you choose to believe?

af.title: Die Held wat Wegkruip
story: Sewe jaar lank het die Midianiete Israel in die oestyd binnegeval. Hulle het met so baie kamele gekom dat hulle nie getel kon word nie, en hulle het alles opgeëet of gevat. God se mense het in grotte in die berge weggekruip.

Gideon was besig om koring in ’n wynpers te dors. Gewoonlik het jy koring bo-op ’n winderige heuwel gedors sodat die wind die kaf kon wegwaai. Gideon het dit onder in ’n gat gedoen om vir die Midianiete weg te kruip. Dit is toe die engel van die Here verskyn het: ‘Die Here is by jou, dapper held.’

Gideon het nie soos ’n dapper held gevoel nie. Hy het met vrae en klagtes geantwoord: ‘As die Here by ons is, hoekom het dit alles gebeur?… My familie is die swakste in Manasse, en ek is die minste in my familie.’
God het nie gestry nie. Hy het eenvoudig gesê: ‘Gaan in die krag wat jy het… Stuur Ek jou nie? Ek sal by jou wees.’

Gideon was steeds nie seker nie. Hy het vir tekens gevra, en God het dit geduldig gegee. Een nag het Gideon ’n wolvel uitgesit en God gevra om dit met dou nat te maak terwyl die grond droog bly. God het dit gedoen. Toe vra Gideon vir die teenoorgestelde, en God het dit ook gedoen.

Let op dat God Gideon ’n ‘dapper held’ genoem het voordat hy enigiets dappers gedoen het. God sien nie net wie ons nou is nie, maar wie ons saam met Hom kan word. Ons moed kom nie daarvandaan dat ons die sterkste of belangrikste is nie. Dit kom van God se belofte: ‘Ek sal by jou wees.’

verse.text: Die Here is by jou, dapper held… Gaan in die krag wat jy het.

lessons: God sien wie ons saam met Hom kan word, nie net wie ons nou is nie.
God is geduldig met ons twyfel en vrae.
Ons moed kom van God se belofte om by ons te wees.
questions: Hoekom het Gideon koring in ’n wynpers gedors?
Hoe het Gideon homself beskryf? Hoe het God hom beskryf?
Wat dink jy noem God jou, selfs as jy dit nie voel nie?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra God: ‘Watter naam noem U my?’ Luister vir ’n woord soos dapper, geliefd, gekies of sterk. Skryf dit neer.
prayer: Here, dankie dat U sien wie ek kan word.
Soms voel ek soos Gideon, veral wanneer…
Help my om te gaan in die krag wat ek het, want U is by my.

mission.text: As jy hierdie week dink ‘Ek kan nie’, herinner jouself: ‘Die Here is by my. Ek kan gaan in die krag wat ek het.’

af.journal: Skryf twee lyste: ‘Wat ek oor myself sê’ en ‘Wat God oor my sê’. Watter lys gaan jy kies om te glo?

en.title: Go in the Strength You Have
story: Judges 6 opens with Israel in a desperate state. Because they had turned to other gods, the Midianites were allowed to oppress them for seven years, invading like locusts every harvest and leaving nothing behind. The people cried out to God, and God answered first with a prophet who reminded them of their unfaithfulness, and then with a calling.

That calling came to a very unlikely person. Gideon is introduced hiding: threshing wheat in a winepress so the raiders won’t see him. The angel’s greeting sounds almost humorous: ‘The Lord is with you, mighty warrior.’

Gideon’s response is honest, even a bit bitter: ‘Pardon me, my lord, but if the Lord is with us, why has all this happened to us? Where are all his wonders?’ God doesn’t rebuke the question. Instead, He turns towards Gideon and says, ‘Go in the strength you have and save Israel… Am I not sending you?’
Gideon objects again: his clan is the weakest, and he is the youngest. God’s answer is the key to the whole story: ‘I will be with you.’ The point was never Gideon’s strength. It was God’s presence.

Gideon’s first assignment is close to home: tear down his own father’s altar to Baal. He obeys, though he does it at night because he is afraid. Courage often starts with one small, frightened act of obedience.

Then comes the famous fleece. Some people treat it as a model for decision-making, but it is better understood as God’s patience with a doubting man who had already been told what to do. God graciously meets Gideon where he is, wet fleece and dry fleece, to strengthen his faith.

Here is the encouragement: God isn’t looking for people who are already brave. He calls people who are willing, names them by what He will make of them, and then goes with them. ‘Mighty warrior’ wasn’t flattery. It was a prophecy.

verse.text: Go in the strength you have… Am I not sending you?… I will be with you.

lessons: God calls us by who we will become with Him.
God welcomes honest questions and is patient with weak faith.
Courage often begins with one small act of obedience, even a frightened one.
questions: What did Gideon’s first act of obedience show about courage?
How do you understand the fleece: a model to copy, or a picture of God’s patience?
Where might God be saying to you, ‘Go in the strength you have’?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Ask God: ‘What small step of obedience are you asking me to take?’ Write down what you sense, even if it feels small.
prayer: Lord, thank you for calling me by who I can become in you.
I have honest questions about…
I will go in the strength I have, because you are with me.

mission.text: Take one small, slightly scary step of obedience this week, even if your knees are shaking.

en.journal: Gideon asked, ‘Where are all His wonders?’ Write your own honest question to God, and then write what you know to be true about Him.

af.title: Gaan in die Krag wat Jy Het
story: Rigters 6 begin met Israel in ’n desperate toestand. Omdat hulle na ander gode gedraai het, is die Midianiete toegelaat om hulle sewe jaar lank te onderdruk, en elke oes soos sprinkane binne te val en niks agter te laat nie. Die mense het na God geroep, en God het eers geantwoord met ’n profeet wat hulle aan hulle ontrouheid herinner het, en toe met ’n roeping.

Daardie roeping het na ’n baie onwaarskynlike persoon gekom. Gideon word aan ons voorgestel terwyl hy wegkruip: hy dors koring in ’n wynpers sodat die rowers hom nie sal sien nie. Die engel se groet klink amper snaaks: ‘Die Here is by jou, dapper held.’

Gideon se antwoord is eerlik, selfs ’n bietjie bitter: ‘Ekskuus, my heer, maar as die Here by ons is, hoekom het dit alles met ons gebeur? Waar is al sy wonders?’ God bestraf nie die vraag nie. In plaas daarvan draai Hy na Gideon en sê: ‘Gaan in die krag wat jy het en red Israel… Stuur Ek jou nie?’

Gideon maak weer beswaar: sy familie is die swakste, en hy is die jongste. God se antwoord is die sleutel tot die hele storie: ‘Ek sal by jou wees.’ Dit het nooit oor Gideon se krag gegaan nie. Dit het oor God se teenwoordigheid gegaan.

Gideon se eerste opdrag is naby die huis: breek sy eie pa se altaar vir Baäl af. Hy gehoorsaam, al doen hy dit in die nag omdat hy bang is. Moed begin dikwels met een klein, bang daad van gehoorsaamheid.

Dan kom die bekende wolvel. Party mense sien dit as ’n voorbeeld vir hoe om besluite te neem, maar dit word beter verstaan as God se geduld met ’n twyfelende man wat reeds gesê is wat om te doen. God ontmoet Gideon genadig waar hy is, nat vel en droë vel, om sy geloof te versterk.

Hier is die bemoediging: God soek nie mense wat reeds dapper is nie. Hy roep mense wat gewillig is, noem hulle na wat Hy van hulle gaan maak, en gaan dan saam met hulle. ‘Dapper held’ was nie vleiery nie. Dit was ’n profesie.

verse.text: Gaan in die krag wat jy het… Stuur Ek jou nie?… Ek sal by jou wees.

lessons: God roep ons na wie ons saam met Hom gaan word.
God verwelkom eerlike vrae en is geduldig met swak geloof.
Moed begin dikwels met een klein daad van gehoorsaamheid, selfs ’n bang een.
questions: Wat het Gideon se eerste daad van gehoorsaamheid oor moed gewys?
Hoe verstaan jy die wolvel: ’n voorbeeld om na te volg, of ’n prentjie van God se geduld?
Waar sê God dalk vir jou: ‘Gaan in die krag wat jy het’?

Ek het eerlike vrae oor…
Ek sal gaan in die krag wat ek het, want U is by my.

af.journal: Gideon het gevra: ‘Waar is al sy wonders?’ Skryf jou eie eerlike vraag aan God, en skryf dan wat jy weet waar is oor Hom.

en.title: God Calls Me Brave

Gideon said, ‘Who, me? I’m not a hero!’
But God said, ‘I will be with you.’

en.action: Hide behind your hands, then jump out like a hero and shout: ‘God is with me!’

questions: Can you show me your strong hero arms?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you are with me. Amen.

af.title: God Noem My Dapper

’n Engel het gekom en gesê: ‘Hallo, dapper held!’

Maar God het gesê: ‘Ek sal by jou wees.’
God sien hoe dapper ons saam met Hom kan wees!

verse.text: Die Here is by jou, dapper held!

af.action: Kruip agter jou hande weg, spring dan uit soos ’n held en roep: ‘God is by my!’

questions: Kan jy vir my jou sterk held-arms wys?
prayer: Liewe God,

en.title: Hello, Mighty Hero!
story: God’s people were in trouble again. Every year, raiders came on camels and took all their food. The people were so frightened that they hid in caves.
A young man called Gideon was secretly threshing wheat (getting the grain ready) inside a winepress, a big hole in the ground, so the raiders wouldn’t see him. He was hiding.
Suddenly an angel of the Lord sat down under a tree nearby and said, ‘The Lord is with you, mighty hero!’
Gideon looked around. Mighty hero? Who, me? ‘My family is the weakest, and I’m the least important in my family!’ he said.
But God said, ‘I will be with you.’ God didn’t see a scared young man hiding in a hole. God saw who Gideon could become with God’s help.

Gideon still had questions, and he asked God for signs. God was patient with him. He put dew on a fleece of wool, and then kept the fleece dry, just as Gideon asked. Step by step, Gideon learned to trust God.
God sees you that way too. He doesn’t only see what you are now. He sees who you can become with Him.

verse.text: The Lord is with you, mighty hero!

lessons: God sees who I can become with His help.
God is patient when I have questions or feel unsure.
My courage comes from God being with me.
questions: Why do you think God called Gideon a ‘mighty hero’ when he was hiding?
What do you think God sees when He looks at you?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you see who I can become.
Thank you for being patient with me.
Help me to trust you, step by step. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, try something you feel a bit unsure about, and remember: ‘The Lord is with me.’

af.title: Hallo, Dapper Held!
story: God se mense was weer in die moeilikheid. Elke jaar het rowers op kamele gekom en al hulle kos gevat. Die mense was so bang dat hulle in grotte weggekruip het.
’n Jong man met die naam Gideon het in die geheim koring in ’n wynpers gedors (die graan reggemaak), ’n groot gat in die grond, sodat die rowers hom nie sou sien nie. Hy het weggekruip.
Skielik het ’n engel van die Here naby onder ’n boom gaan sit en gesê: ‘Die Here is by jou, dapper held!’
Gideon het rondgekyk. Dapper held? Wie, ek? ‘My familie is die swakste, en ek is die onbelangrikste in my familie!’ het hy gesê.
Maar God het gesê: ‘Ek sal by jou wees.’ God het nie ’n bang jong man gesien wat in ’n gat wegkruip nie. God het gesien wie Gideon met God se hulp kon word.

Gideon het nog vrae gehad, en hy het God vir tekens gevra. God was geduldig met hom. Hy het dou op ’n wolvel gesit, en toe die vel droog gehou, net soos Gideon gevra het. Tree vir tree het Gideon geleer om God te vertrou.
God sien jou ook so. Hy sien nie net wat jy nou is nie. Hy sien wie jy saam met Hom kan word.

lessons: God sien wie ek met sy hulp kan word.
God is geduldig as ek vrae het of onseker voel.
My moed kom daarvandaan dat God by my is.
questions: Hoekom dink jy het God vir Gideon ’n ‘dapper held’ genoem toe hy weggekruip het?
Wat dink jy sien God as Hy na jou kyk?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U sien wie ek kan word.
Dankie dat U geduldig is met my.
Help my om U te vertrou, tree vir tree. Amen.

mission.text: Probeer môre iets waaroor jy ’n bietjie onseker voel, en onthou: ‘Die Here is by my.’

trait.en: The victory comes from God
trait.af: Die oorwinning kom van God

en.title: Three Hundred Torches
story: Gideon gathered thirty-two thousand men to fight the Midianites, whose army was ‘as thick as locusts’. You might expect God to say, ‘Good, but you need more!’ Instead God said, ‘You have too many men.’
God explained why: if Israel won with a large army, they would boast, ‘My own strength has saved me.’ God wanted everyone to know that the victory came from Him.

First, God told Gideon to send home anyone who was afraid. Twenty-two thousand left. Then God tested the remaining ten thousand at the water. Only the three hundred who lapped water from their hands were kept. The army was now less than one percent of its original size!

God knew Gideon was nervous, so He sent him on a secret night mission into the enemy camp. There Gideon overheard a soldier describing a dream about a loaf of bread rolling into the camp and knocking over a tent. His friend said, ‘This can be nothing other than the sword of Gideon… God has given the Midianites into his hands.’ Gideon worshipped right there.

Then he divided his men into three groups. Each man had a trumpet and an empty jar with a torch inside. At Gideon’s signal they blew the trumpets, smashed the jars and shouted, ‘A sword for the Lord and for Gideon!’ The Midianites panicked, turned on each other in the dark, and fled.

Gideon’s army didn’t win because they were strong. They won because God was with them, and everyone knew it. When you feel small, remember: God doesn’t need big numbers. He needs people who trust Him.

verse.text: ‘Not by might nor by power, but by my Spirit,’ says the Lord Almighty.

lessons: God sometimes makes us smaller so that His power is seen.
God encourages us when we are nervous.
The victory belongs to God, so the glory belongs to Him too.
questions: Why did God want a smaller army?
How did God encourage Gideon before the battle?
When have you seen God do something that you could never have done on your own?
en.listen: Be still and ask: ‘Lord, where am I trying to win by my own strength?’ Listen, and write down what you sense.
prayer: Lord, thank you that you don’t need me to be big or strong.
I need your strength for…
When you help me, I will give you the glory.

mission.text: This week, when something goes well, tell someone how God helped you.

en.journal: Draw a jar with light shining out of a crack. Write 2 Corinthians 4:7 next to it: ‘We have this treasure in jars of clay.’

af.title: Driehonderd Fakkels
story: Gideon het twee-en-dertig duisend mans bymekaargemaak om teen die Midianiete te veg, wie se leër ‘so dig soos sprinkane’ was. Jy sou verwag God sê: ‘Goed, maar jy het meer nodig!’ In plaas daarvan het God gesê: ‘Jy het te veel mans.’
God het verduidelik hoekom: as Israel met ’n groot leër wen, sou hulle spog: ‘My eie krag het my gered.’ God wou hê almal moet weet dat die oorwinning van Hom kom.

Eers het God vir Gideon gesê om enigiemand wat bang is, huis toe te stuur. Twee-en-twintig duisend het gegaan. Toe het God die oorblywende tienduisend by die water getoets. Net die driehonderd wat water uit hulle hande opgelek het, is gehou. Die leër was nou minder as een persent van sy oorspronklike grootte!

God het geweet Gideon is senuweeagtig, toe stuur Hy hom op ’n geheime nagsending na die vyand se kamp. Daar het Gideon gehoor hoe ’n soldaat ’n droom vertel oor ’n brood wat die kamp in rol en ’n tent omstamp. Sy vriend het gesê: ‘Dit kan niks anders wees as die swaard van Gideon nie… God het die Midianiete in sy hand gegee.’ Gideon het net daar aanbid.

Toe het hy sy mans in drie groepe verdeel. Elke man het ’n trompet gehad en ’n leë kruik met ’n fakkel daarin. Op Gideon se teken het hulle die trompette geblaas, die kruike stukkend geslaan en geroep: ‘’n Swaard vir die Here en vir Gideon!’ Die Midianiete het paniekerig geraak, mekaar in die donker aangeval, en gevlug.

Gideon se leër het nie gewen omdat hulle sterk was nie. Hulle het gewen omdat God by hulle was, en almal het dit geweet. As jy klein voel, onthou: God het nie groot getalle nodig nie. Hy het mense nodig wat Hom vertrou.

verse.text: ‘Nie deur mag of deur krag nie, maar deur my Gees,’ sê die Here die Almagtige.

lessons: God maak ons soms kleiner sodat sy krag gesien kan word.
God bemoedig ons as ons senuweeagtig is.
Die oorwinning behoort aan God, dus behoort die eer ook aan Hom.
questions: Hoekom wou God ’n kleiner leër hê?
Hoe het God vir Gideon voor die geveg bemoedig?
Wanneer het jy al gesien God doen iets wat jy nooit self sou kon doen nie?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra: ‘Here, waar probeer ek deur my eie krag wen?’ Luister, en skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Here, dankie dat U nie nodig het dat ek groot of sterk is nie.
Ek het u krag nodig vir…
As U my help, sal ek U die eer gee.

mission.text: Vertel hierdie week, as iets goed gaan, vir iemand hoe God jou gehelp het.

af.journal: Teken ’n kruik met lig wat deur ’n kraak skyn. Skryf 2 Korintiërs 4:7 langsaan: ‘Ons wat hierdie skat het, is soos kleipotte.’

en.title: Too Many to Win
story: Judges 7 is a lesson in God’s strange mathematics. Gideon musters thirty-two thousand men against a Midianite army described as ‘thick as locusts’ with ‘camels as numerous as the sand on the seashore’. By any human calculation, he needs more soldiers. God says he has too many.

God gives the reason plainly: ‘in order that Israel may not boast against me that her own strength has saved her’. God isn’t against effort or strategy. He is against pride, the attitude that takes the credit for what God has done. So He reduces the army in two stages: first those who are afraid go home (twenty-two thousand!), then those who kneel to drink. Three hundred remain.

Notice God’s kindness to Gideon in the middle of this. He says, ‘If you are afraid to attack, go down to the camp’, and lets Gideon overhear a Midianite soldier’s dream that predicts their defeat. God doesn’t shame Gideon’s fear; He feeds his faith. And Gideon’s response is worship, before the battle has even begun.

The weapons are almost absurd: trumpets, clay jars and torches. The jars hide the light until the moment they are broken. Then three hundred lights blaze out on three sides, trumpets blast and the shout goes up. In the confusion the Midianite army turns on itself.

Centuries later Paul used the same picture: ‘God… made his light shine in our hearts… But we have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this all-surpassing power is from God and not from us.’ We are the clay jars: ordinary, fragile, sometimes cracked. But God’s light lives in us, and it often shines most clearly through our cracks and weaknesses.

In a culture that tells you to be impressive, self-sufficient and strong, this story says something freeing: you don’t have to be enough. God is enough. Your part is to trust, obey and let His light out.

verse.text: We have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this all-surpassing power is from God and not from us.

lessons: God works in ways that make it clear the power is His, not ours.
God feeds our faith when we are afraid, instead of shaming us.
We are clay jars holding God’s light; our weaknesses can let it shine.
questions: Why does pride concern God so much in this story?
How did God help Gideon with his fear?
What do you think it means that God’s light shines through our ‘cracks’?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Ask God: ‘Where do you want your light to shine through my weakness?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: God, thank you that I don’t have to be enough, because you are.
I feel weak or small in…
Let your light shine through me, cracks and all.

mission.text: This week, be honest with a friend about something you find hard, and tell them how God is helping you.

en.journal: Draw a clay jar with cracks. Label each crack with a weakness, and draw God’s light shining through each one.

af.title: Te Veel om te Wen
story: Rigters 7 is ’n les in God se vreemde wiskunde. Gideon maak twee-en-dertig duisend mans bymekaar teen ’n Midianitiese leër wat beskryf word as ‘so dig soos sprinkane’ met ‘kamele so baie soos die sand by die see’. Volgens enige menslike berekening het hy meer soldate nodig. God sê hy het te veel.

God gee die rede duidelik: ‘sodat Israel nie teen My kan spog dat hulle eie krag hulle gered het nie’. God is nie teen harde werk of ’n goeie plan nie. Hy is teen trots, die houding wat die eer vat vir wat God gedoen het. So maak Hy die leër in twee stappe kleiner: eers gaan die wat bang is huis toe (twee-en-twintig duisend!), toe die wat kniel om te drink. Driehonderd bly oor.

Let op God se goedheid teenoor Gideon in die middel van dit alles. Hy sê: ‘As jy bang is om aan te val, gaan af na die kamp’, en laat Gideon ’n Midianitiese soldaat se droom hoor wat hulle nederlaag voorspel. God laat Gideon nie skaam voel oor sy vrees nie; Hy voed sy geloof. En Gideon se reaksie is aanbidding, nog voordat die geveg begin het.

Die wapens is amper belaglik: trompette, kleikruike en fakkels. Die kruike steek die lig weg tot die oomblik dat hulle gebreek word. Dan vlam driehonderd ligte aan drie kante op, trompette blaas en die geroep gaan op. In die verwarring draai die Midianitiese leër teen homself.

Eeue later het Paulus dieselfde prentjie gebruik: ‘God… het sy lig in ons harte laat skyn… Maar ons wat hierdie skat het, is soos kleipotte, sodat dit duidelik kan wees dat die oorweldigende krag van God kom en nie van ons nie.’ Ons is die kleipotte: gewoon, breekbaar, soms gekraak. Maar God se lig woon in ons, en dit skyn dikwels die helderste deur ons krake en swakhede.

In ’n kultuur wat vir jou sê om indrukwekkend, selfstandig en sterk te wees, sê hierdie storie iets wat vry maak: jy hoef nie genoeg te wees nie. God is genoeg. Jou deel is om te vertrou, te gehoorsaam en sy lig te laat uitskyn.

verse.text: Ons wat hierdie skat het, is soos kleipotte, sodat dit duidelik kan wees dat die oorweldigende krag van God kom en nie van ons nie.

lessons: God werk op maniere wat dit duidelik maak dat die krag syne is, nie ons s’n nie.
God voed ons geloof as ons bang is, in plaas daarvan om ons skaam te laat voel.
Ons is kleipotte wat God se lig dra; ons swakhede kan dit laat skyn.
questions: Hoekom is trots vir God so ’n groot saak in hierdie storie?
Hoe het God Gideon met sy vrees gehelp?
Wat dink jy beteken dit dat God se lig deur ons ‘krake’ skyn?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Vra God: ‘Waar wil U hê u lig moet deur my swakheid skyn?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, dankie dat ek nie genoeg hoef te wees nie, want U is.
Ek voel swak of klein in…
Laat u lig deur my skyn, krake en al.

mission.text: Wees hierdie week eerlik met ’n maat oor iets wat jy moeilik vind, en vertel hulle hoe God jou help.

af.journal: Teken ’n kleipot met krake. Skryf by elke kraak ’n swakheid, en teken hoe God se lig deur elkeen skyn.

en.title: God Wins
story: Gideon had only a few soldiers.
They had trumpets and jars with lights inside.
In the night they blew the trumpets: toot, toot! They broke the jars: crash!
The lights shone, and the enemies ran away!
God won the battle. God is strong!

verse.text: Not by might, but by my Spirit, says the Lord.

en.action: Blow a pretend trumpet: toot, toot! Then hold up your hands like shining lights.
lessons: God is strong, and He helps me.
questions: Can you make a trumpet sound?
prayer: Dear God,
you are so strong! Amen.

af.title: God Wen
story: Gideon het net ’n paar soldate gehad.
Hulle het trompette en kruike met ligte binne-in gehad.
In die nag het hulle die trompette geblaas: toet, toet! Hulle het die kruike gebreek: kraak!
Die ligte het geskyn, en die vyande het weggehardloop!
God het die geveg gewen. God is sterk!

verse.text: Nie deur mag nie, maar deur my Gees, sê die Here.

af.action: Blaas ’n speel-trompet: toet, toet! Hou dan jou hande op soos ligte wat skyn.
lessons: God is sterk, en Hy help my.
questions: Kan jy ’n trompetgeluid maak?
prayer: Liewe God,
U is so sterk! Amen.

en.title: Trumpets, Jars and Torches
story: Gideon gathered an army of thirty-two thousand men. But God said, ‘You have too many!’ Too many? The enemy army was so big it was like a swarm of locusts!
God explained: ‘If you win with a big army, the people will think they won by their own strength.’ So God told Gideon to send home everyone who was afraid. Twenty-two thousand men went home!
Then God said, ‘Still too many.’ He tested the men at the water. In the end, only three hundred men were left.
That night Gideon gave each man a strange weapon: a trumpet, and a clay jar with a burning torch hidden inside. Quietly they surrounded the enemy camp.
Gideon blew his trumpet. Then all three hundred men blew their trumpets, smashed their jars, held up their torches and shouted, ‘A sword for the Lord and for Gideon!’
The enemy woke up in a fright. All they could see was lights and all they could hear was trumpets. They panicked and ran away! God had won the battle.
God doesn’t need us to be big or strong. When we are small and trust Him, everyone can see that the victory comes from God.

verse.text: ‘Not by might nor by power, but by my Spirit,’ says the Lord.

lessons: The victory comes from God, not from how big or strong I am.
God can do great things with a few people who trust Him.
When God helps me, I can give Him the thanks.
questions: Why did God want Gideon to have a small army?
What is something too big for you that you can trust God with?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you don’t need me to be big.
When things feel too big for me,
help me to trust your strength. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, when you do something well, say: ‘Thank you, God, for helping me!’

af.title: Trompette, Kruike en Fakkels
story: Gideon het ’n leër van twee-en-dertig duisend mans bymekaargemaak. Maar God het gesê: ‘Jy het te veel!’ Te veel? Die vyand se leër was so groot dat dit soos ’n swerm sprinkane was!

God het verduidelik: ‘As jy met ’n groot leër wen, sal die mense dink hulle het deur hulle eie krag gewen.’ Toe het God vir Gideon gesê om almal wat bang is, huis toe te stuur. Twee-en-twintig duisend mans het huis toe gegaan!
Toe sê God: ‘Nog steeds te veel.’ Hy het die mans by die water getoets. Op die ou end was daar net driehonderd mans oor.
Daardie nag het Gideon vir elke man ’n vreemde wapen gegee: ’n trompet, en ’n kleikruik met ’n brandende fakkel daarin weggesteek. Stil-stil het hulle die vyand se kamp omsingel.
Gideon het sy trompet geblaas. Toe het al driehonderd mans hulle trompette geblaas, hulle kruike stukkend geslaan, hulle fakkels opgehou en geroep: ‘’n Swaard vir die Here en vir Gideon!’
Die vyand het groot geskrik wakker geword. Al wat hulle kon sien, was ligte, en al wat hulle kon hoor, was trompette. Hulle het paniekerig weggehardloop! God het die geveg gewen.
God het nie nodig dat ons groot of sterk moet wees nie. As ons klein is en Hom vertrou, kan almal sien dat die oorwinning van God kom.

verse.text: ‘Nie deur mag of deur krag nie, maar deur my Gees,’ sê die Here.

lessons: Die oorwinning kom van God, nie van hoe groot of sterk ek is nie.
God kan groot dinge doen met ’n paar mense wat Hom vertrou.
As God my help, kan ek Hom die dank gee.
questions: Hoekom wou God hê Gideon moet ’n klein leër hê?
Wat is iets wat vir jou te groot is wat jy vir God kan toevertrou?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U nie nodig het dat ek groot is nie.
As dinge vir my te groot voel,
help my om u krag te vertrou. Amen.

mission.text: As jy môre iets goed doen, sê: ‘Dankie, God, dat U my help!’

en.title: Trumpets, Jars and Torches
story: Gideon gathered an army of thirty-two thousand men. But God said, ‘You have too many!’ Too many? The enemy army was so big it was like a swarm of locusts!
God explained: ‘If you win with a big army, the people will think they won by their own strength.’ So God told Gideon to send home everyone who was afraid. Twenty-two thousand men went home!
Then God said, ‘Still too many.’ He tested the men at the water. In the end, only three hundred men were left.
That night Gideon gave each man a strange weapon: a trumpet, and a clay jar with a burning torch hidden inside. Quietly they surrounded the enemy camp.
Gideon blew his trumpet. Then all three hundred men blew their trumpets, smashed their jars, held up their torches and shouted, ‘A sword for the Lord and for Gideon!’
The enemy woke up in a fright. All they could see was lights and all they could hear was trumpets. They panicked and ran away! God had won the battle.
God doesn’t need us to be big or strong. When we are small and trust Him, everyone can see that the victory comes from God.

verse.text: ‘Not by might nor by power, but by my Spirit,’ says the Lord.

lessons: The victory comes from God, not from how big or strong I am.
God can do great things with a few people who trust Him.
When God helps me, I can give Him the thanks.
questions: Why did God want Gideon to have a small army?
What is something too big for you that you can trust God with?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you don’t need me to be big.
When things feel too big for me,
help me to trust your strength. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, when you do something well, say: ‘Thank you, God, for helping me!’

en.fact: Gideon’s army went from 32 000 men to only 300. That means for every 100 soldiers, only 1 was left!
en.deeper: How do you think the 300 men felt when they saw how many enemies there were?
en.journal: Draw a trumpet, a jar and a torch. Next to them, write Zechariah 4:6.

en.title: Hannah Pours Out Her Heart
story: Every year, Elkanah took his family to worship at Shiloh. For his wife Hannah, it was the hardest trip of the year. She had no children, and Elkanah’s other wife, Peninnah, who had many children, would tease her until she cried and couldn’t eat.
Elkanah loved Hannah and tried to comfort her: ‘Don’t I mean more to you than ten sons?’ But her pain went deeper than words could fix.

So Hannah took it to God. Standing in the temple, ‘in her deep anguish Hannah prayed to the Lord, weeping bitterly.’ She prayed so deeply that her lips moved but no sound came out. She promised that if God gave her a son, she would give him back to serve the Lord all his life.

Eli the priest was watching and thought she was drunk! Hannah explained, ‘I was pouring out my soul to the Lord.’ Eli blessed her: ‘Go in peace, and may the God of Israel grant you what you have asked.’
The Bible says Hannah ‘went her way and ate something, and her face was no longer downcast’. Notice that her circumstances hadn’t changed yet, but her heart had. She had given her burden to God.

God remembered Hannah. She gave birth to a son and named him Samuel. When he was old enough, she kept her promise and brought him to serve with Eli. Then Hannah sang a song of praise: ‘My heart rejoices in the Lord!’
God wants to hear the deep things in your heart too: your disappointments, your longings and your hurts. You can pour them all out to Him.

verse.text: Trust in Him at all times… pour out your hearts to Him, for God is our refuge.

lessons: We can pour out our deepest feelings to God.
Prayer can bring peace even before circumstances change.
God remembers us and hears our cries.
questions: How did Peninnah make Hannah’s pain worse?
What changed in Hannah after she prayed?
Is there something deep in your heart you have never told God?
en.listen: Be still. Tell God honestly about something that hurts or something you long for. Then ask: ‘Lord, what do you want to say to me about this?’ Write it down.
prayer: Lord, thank you that I can pour out my heart to you.
The deepest thing in my heart right now is…
Please give me your peace.

mission.text: This week, write God a letter about something you’ve kept inside, and give it to Him in prayer.

en.journal: Write your own ‘Hannah prayer’: tell God about a longing or hurt, and finish with ‘My heart rejoices in the Lord because…’

af.title: Hanna Stort Haar Hart Uit
story: Elke jaar het Elkana sy familie na Silo geneem om te aanbid. Vir sy vrou Hanna was dit die moeilikste reis van die jaar. Sy het geen kinders gehad nie, en Elkana se ander vrou, Peninna, wat baie kinders gehad het, het haar gespot totdat sy gehuil en nie kon eet nie.
Elkana het Hanna liefgehad en probeer om haar te troos: ‘Beteken ek nie vir jou meer as tien seuns nie?’ Maar haar pyn was dieper as wat woorde kon regmaak.

Toe het Hanna dit na God geneem. Terwyl sy in die tempel staan, ‘het Hanna in haar diepe hartseer tot die Here gebid en bitterlik gehuil.’ Sy het so diep gebid dat haar lippe beweeg het, maar geen geluid uitgekom het nie. Sy het belowe dat as God vir haar ’n seun gee, sy hom sou teruggee om die Here sy hele lewe lank te dien.

Eli die priester het gekyk en gedink sy is dronk! Hanna het verduidelik: ‘Ek het my siel by die Here uitgestort.’ Eli het haar geseën: ‘Gaan in vrede, en mag die God van Israel jou gee wat jy gevra het.’
Die Bybel sê Hanna ‘het gegaan en iets geëet, en haar gesig was nie meer bedruk nie’. Let op dat haar omstandighede nog nie verander het nie, maar haar hart het. Sy het haar las vir God gegee.

God het Hanna onthou. Sy het geboorte gegee aan ’n seun en hom Samuel genoem. Toe hy oud genoeg was, het sy haar belofte gehou en hom gebring om saam met Eli te dien. Toe het Hanna ’n loflied gesing: ‘My hart is bly in die Here!’
God wil ook die diep dinge in jou hart hoor: jou teleurstellings, jou verlangens en jou seer. Jy kan dit alles by Hom uitstort.

verse.text: Vertrou altyd op Hom… stort jou hart voor Hom uit, want God is ons toevlug.

lessons: Ons kan ons diepste gevoelens by God uitstort.
Gebed kan vrede bring selfs voordat omstandighede verander.
God onthou ons en hoor ons roep.
questions: Hoe het Peninna Hanna se pyn erger gemaak?
Wat het in Hanna verander nadat sy gebid het?
Is daar iets diep in jou hart wat jy nog nooit vir God vertel het nie?
af.listen: Wees stil. Vertel God eerlik van iets wat seer is of iets waarna jy verlang. Vra dan: ‘Here, wat wil U vir my hieroor sê?’ Skryf dit neer.
prayer: Here, dankie dat ek my hart by U kan uitstort.
Die diepste ding in my hart nou is…
Gee my asseblief u vrede.

mission.text: Skryf hierdie week vir God ’n brief oor iets wat jy binne-in gehou het, en gee dit in gebed vir Hom.

af.journal: Skryf jou eie ‘Hanna-gebed’: vertel God van ’n verlange of seer, en eindig met ‘My hart is bly in die Here omdat…’

en.title: Honest Prayer and Deep Peace
story: The book of Samuel, which tells the story of Israel’s first kings, begins not in a palace but in the heart of a hurting woman. That says something about where God pays attention.

Hannah lives with a deep sorrow. In her culture, a woman without children was often looked down on, and Peninnah uses this to provoke her ‘year after year’. Elkanah’s love is real, but his question, ‘Don’t I mean more to you than ten sons?’, shows that he doesn’t fully understand. Sometimes even the people who love us can’t reach the deepest place of our pain.

Hannah takes that pain to God. Look at the words used: ‘deep anguish’, ‘weeping bitterly’, ‘pouring out my soul’, ‘great anguish and grief’. Her prayer isn’t polite or tidy. It is raw honesty, and God welcomes it. The Psalms are full of prayers like this. God would rather have our honest tears than our pretend smiles.

Then something remarkable happens. After Eli’s blessing, ‘she went her way and ate something, and her face was no longer downcast’. Nothing had changed on the outside. She wasn’t pregnant yet. But she had placed her burden in God’s hands, and she received His peace. Paul describes the same thing: ‘Do not be anxious about anything, but in every situation, by prayer… present your requests to God. And the peace of God… will guard your hearts.’

God answered, and Samuel was born. Hannah kept her vow and dedicated Samuel to the Lord. Her song in chapter 2 is one of the great songs of the Bible. She celebrates a God who ‘raises the poor from the dust’ and turns things upside down. Mary, the mother of Jesus, would sing a very similar song a thousand years later.
Not every prayer is answered the way Hannah’s was. But every honest prayer is heard, and God’s peace is available even while we wait.

verse.text: Present your requests to God. And the peace of God, which transcends all understanding, will guard your hearts.

lessons: God welcomes raw, honest prayer, not only polite words.
God’s peace can guard our hearts even before our circumstances change.
God notices the overlooked and lifts up the humble.
questions: Why do you think the story of Israel’s kings begins with Hannah?
How did Hannah’s face change before her situation changed?
Do you find it easy or hard to be honest with God about your feelings? Why?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Pour out to God whatever is heaviest on your heart. Then sit quietly and ask for His peace. Write down what you notice.
prayer: God, here is what is really in my heart: …
I place this burden in your hands.
Thank you for your peace that guards my heart.

mission.text: This week, when you feel anxious, follow Philippians 4:6: name it, ask God for help, thank Him, and receive His peace.

en.journal: Read Hannah’s song (1 Samuel 2:1–10) and Mary’s song (Luke 1:46–55). Write down three things they both say about God.

af.title: Eerlike Gebed en Diep Vrede
story: Die boek Samuel, wat die storie van Israel se eerste konings vertel, begin nie in ’n paleis nie, maar in die hart van ’n vrou wat seerkry. Dit sê iets oor waar God aandag gee.

Hanna lewe met ’n diep hartseer. In haar kultuur is daar dikwels op ’n vrou sonder kinders neergesien, en Peninna gebruik dit om haar ‘jaar na jaar’ te terg. Elkana se liefde is eg, maar sy vraag, ‘Beteken ek nie vir jou meer as tien seuns nie?’, wys dat hy nie heeltemal verstaan nie. Soms kan selfs die mense wat ons liefhet, nie die diepste plek van ons pyn bereik nie.

Hanna neem daardie pyn na God. Kyk na die woorde wat gebruik word: ‘diepe hartseer’, ‘bitterlik gehuil’, ‘my siel uitgestort’, ‘groot angs en verdriet’. Haar gebed is nie beleefd of netjies nie. Dit is rou eerlikheid, en God verwelkom dit. Die Psalms is vol gebede soos hierdie. God sal eerder ons eerlike trane hê as ons gemaakte glimlagte.

Dan gebeur iets merkwaardigs. Ná Eli se seën ‘het sy gegaan en iets geëet, en haar gesig was nie meer bedruk nie’. Niks het van buite verander nie. Sy was nog nie swanger nie. Maar sy het haar las in God se hande gelê, en sy het sy vrede ontvang. Paulus beskryf dieselfde ding: ‘Moet oor niks besorg wees nie, maar bring in elke situasie julle versoeke in gebed by God. En die vrede van God… sal julle harte bewaak.’

God het geantwoord, en Samuel is gebore. Hanna het haar gelofte gehou en Samuel aan die Here toegewy. Haar lied in hoofstuk 2 is een van die groot liedere van die Bybel. Sy vier ’n God wat ‘die arme uit die stof ophef’ en dinge onderstebo keer. Maria, die moeder van Jesus, sou duisend jaar later ’n baie soortgelyke lied sing.
Nie elke gebed word beantwoord soos Hanna s’n nie. Maar elke eerlike gebed word gehoor, en God se vrede is beskikbaar selfs terwyl ons wag.

verse.text: Bring julle versoeke by God. En die vrede van God, wat alle verstand te bowe gaan, sal julle harte bewaak.

lessons: God verwelkom rou, eerlike gebed, nie net beleefde woorde nie.
God se vrede kan ons harte bewaak selfs voordat ons omstandighede verander.
God sien die oor-die-hoof-gesienes raak en hef die nederiges op.
questions: Hoekom dink jy begin die storie van Israel se konings met Hanna?
Hoe het Hanna se gesig verander voordat haar situasie verander het?
Vind jy dit maklik of moeilik om eerlik met God oor jou gevoelens te wees? Hoekom?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Stort by God uit wat die swaarste op jou hart lê. Sit dan stil en vra vir sy vrede. Skryf neer wat jy agterkom.
prayer: God, hier is wat regtig in my hart is: …
Ek lê hierdie las in u hande.
Dankie vir u vrede wat my hart bewaak.

mission.text: Volg hierdie week, as jy angstig voel, Filippense 4:6: noem dit, vra God vir hulp, dank Hom, en ontvang sy vrede.

af.journal: Lees Hanna se lied (1 Samuel 2:1–10) en Maria se lied (Lukas 1:46–55). Skryf drie dinge neer wat albei oor God sê.

en.title: God Hears Me
story: Hannah was very sad. She wanted a baby so much.
She went to God’s house and prayed and cried.
God heard Hannah’s prayer!
God gave her a baby boy called Samuel.
God hears me when I pray.

verse.text: The Lord hears me when I call to Him.

en.action: Cup your hand around your ear like you’re listening, and say: ‘God hears me!’
lessons: God hears me when I pray.
questions: What would you like to tell God tonight?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you hear me. Amen.

af.title: God Hoor My
story: Hanna was baie hartseer. Sy wou so graag ’n baba hê.
Sy het na God se huis gegaan en gebid en gehuil.
God het Hanna se gebed gehoor!
God het vir haar ’n babaseuntjie gegee met die naam Samuel.
God hoor my as ek bid.

verse.text: Die Here hoor my as ek na Hom roep.

af.action: Hou jou hand agter jou oor asof jy luister, en sê: ‘God hoor my!’
lessons: God hoor my as ek bid.
questions: Wat wil jy vanaand vir God vertel?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U my hoor. Amen.

prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you hear my heart.
Tonight I want to tell you…

mission.text: Tomorrow, find a quiet moment and tell God something that is deep in your heart.

en.title: Josiah: Young and Wholehearted
story: Josiah became king of Judah when he was just eight years old, about your age! His grandfather Manasseh had been one of the worst kings in history, filling the land with idols. His father Amon had followed the same path and ruled for only two years.

So Josiah grew up in a palace where God had been forgotten. Yet 2 Chronicles tells us that when he was sixteen, ‘he began to seek the God of his father David’. Nobody forced him. He chose to seek God for himself.

When Josiah was twenty-six, he ordered the neglected temple to be repaired. During the work, the high priest Hilkiah made an incredible discovery: ‘I have found the Book of the Law in the temple of the Lord!’ God’s Word had been lost, probably for decades.

When the scroll was read to Josiah, he tore his robes, a sign of deep sorrow. He realised how far the nation had drifted from God. He didn’t make excuses. He humbled himself, and God said, ‘Because your heart was responsive and you humbled yourself… I have heard you.’

Then Josiah gathered all the people, ‘from the least to the greatest’, and read the whole book to them. He made a covenant ‘to follow the Lord and keep His commands… with all his heart and all his soul’. He cleared the land of idols and led the greatest Passover celebration in centuries.
Josiah shows us that you are never too young to seek God, and that God’s Word has the power to change hearts and even a whole nation.

verse.text: Don’t let anyone look down on you because you are young, but set an example… in faith.

lessons: You are never too young to seek God for yourself.

af.title: Josia: Jonk en met sy Hele Hart
story: Josia het koning van Juda geword toe hy net agt jaar oud was, omtrent so oud soos jy! Sy oupa Manasse was een van die slegste konings in die geskiedenis, en het die land met afgode gevul. Sy pa Amon het dieselfde pad gevolg en net twee jaar lank regeer.

So het Josia grootgeword in ’n paleis waar God vergeet is. Tog vertel 2 Kronieke ons dat toe hy sestien was, ‘hy begin het om die God van sy voorvader Dawid te soek’. Niemand het hom gedwing nie. Hy het self gekies om God te soek.

Toe Josia ses-en-twintig was, het hy beveel dat die verwaarloosde tempel herstel word. Tydens die werk het die hoëpriester Hilkia ’n ongelooflike ontdekking gemaak: ‘Ek het die Boek van die Wet in die tempel van die Here gekry!’ God se Woord was verlore, waarskynlik vir dekades.

Toe die boekrol vir Josia voorgelees is, het hy sy klere geskeur, ’n teken van diep hartseer. Hy het besef hoe ver die volk van God af weggedryf het. Hy het nie verskonings gemaak nie. Hy het homself verneder, en God het gesê: ‘Omdat jou hart ontvanklik was en jy jou verneder het… het Ek jou gehoor.’

Toe het Josia al die mense bymekaargemaak, ‘van die kleinste tot die grootste’, en die hele boek vir hulle voorgelees. Hy het ’n verbond gesluit ‘om die Here te volg en sy gebooie te hou… met sy hele hart en sy hele siel’. Hy het die land van afgode skoongemaak en die grootste Paasfees in eeue gelei.
Josia wys vir ons dat jy nooit te jonk is om God te soek nie, en dat God se Woord die krag het om harte, en selfs ’n hele volk, te verander.

en.title: Rediscovering the Book
story: Josiah’s story is one of the most hopeful in the history of Israel’s kings. It shows that a single generation can turn back to God, even after decades of darkness, and that young people can lead the way.

Consider his background. His grandfather Manasseh reigned for fifty-five years and was so wicked that he even sacrificed his own son. His father Amon continued that evil until he was assassinated. Josiah was crowned at eight. Humanly speaking, he had every reason to repeat the family pattern.

But 2 Chronicles 34:3 records a turning point: ‘In the eighth year of his reign, while he was still young, he began to seek the God of his father David.’ At about sixteen, he made a personal decision. Faith can be passed on by families, but each of us must also make it our own.

Ten years later, during temple repairs, the high priest finds ‘the Book of the Law’, most likely Deuteronomy. Think about that: God’s own Word had been lost inside God’s own house. It is possible to be surrounded by religion and still be out of touch with what God has actually said.

Josiah’s reaction is the heart of the story. He tears his robes in grief. He doesn’t defend himself or blame his ancestors. He sends to ask the prophetess Huldah what God is saying. God’s reply is personal: ‘Because your heart was responsive and you humbled yourself before the Lord… I have heard you.’

Then he acts. He reads the whole book aloud to the nation, renews the covenant, removes the idols from Jerusalem to Bethel and celebrates the Passover. 2 Kings 23:25 gives him a remarkable verdict: ‘Neither before nor after Josiah was there a king like him who turned to the Lord as he did, with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his strength.’

What about you? You might come from a family where faith is strong, or one where it is missing. Either way, you can seek God for yourself, let His Word shape you, and make a difference to the people around you.

verse.text: Don’t let anyone look down on you because you are young, but set an example for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith and in purity.

lessons: Each person must make faith their own, whatever their background.
It is possible to be surrounded by religion and still miss what God has said.
A humble, responsive heart to God’s Word can change a generation.
questions: What does it mean that God’s Word was lost inside God’s house? Could something similar happen today?
Why do you think God valued Josiah’s responsive heart so much?
In which of the five areas of 1 Timothy 4:12 could you set an example?

af.title: Die Boek Herontdek
story: Josia se storie is een van die mees hoopvolle in die geskiedenis van Israel se konings. Dit wys dat ’n enkele geslag kan terugdraai na God, selfs ná dekades van donkerte, en dat jong mense die pad kan wys.

Dink aan sy agtergrond. Sy oupa Manasse het vyf-en-vyftig jaar lank regeer en was so goddeloos dat hy selfs sy eie seun geoffer het. Sy pa Amon het met daardie kwaad voortgegaan totdat hy vermoor is. Josia is op agt gekroon. Menslik gesproke het hy elke rede gehad om die familiepatroon te herhaal.

Maar 2 Kronieke 34:3 skryf ’n keerpunt op: ‘In die agtste jaar van sy regering, terwyl hy nog jonk was, het hy begin om die God van sy voorvader Dawid te soek.’ Op omtrent sestien het hy ’n persoonlike besluit geneem. Geloof kan deur families oorgedra word, maar elkeen van ons moet dit ook ons eie maak.

Tien jaar later, tydens herstelwerk aan die tempel, kry die hoëpriester ‘die Boek van die Wet’, heel waarskynlik Deuteronomium. Dink daaroor: God se eie Woord was in God se eie huis verlore. Dit is moontlik om deur godsdiens omring te wees en tog nie te weet wat God eintlik gesê het nie.

Josia se reaksie is die hart van die storie. Hy skeur sy klere van hartseer. Hy verdedig homself nie en blameer nie sy voorouers nie. Hy stuur om die profetes Hulda te vra wat God sê. God se antwoord is persoonlik: ‘Omdat jou hart ontvanklik was en jy jou voor die Here verneder het… het Ek jou gehoor.’

Dan tree hy op. Hy lees die hele boek hardop vir die volk voor, hernu die verbond, verwyder die afgode van Jerusalem tot by Bet-El en vier die Paasfees. 2 Konings 23:25 gee hom ’n merkwaardige uitspraak: ‘Voor of ná Josia was daar nie ’n koning soos hy wat hom na die Here gedraai het soos hy, met sy hele hart en met sy hele siel en met al sy krag nie.’
En jy? Jy kom dalk uit ’n familie waar geloof sterk is, of een waar dit ontbreek. Hoe dit ook al sy, jy kan God self soek, sy Woord jou laat vorm, en ’n verskil maak aan die mense rondom jou.

lessons: Elke mens moet geloof sy eie maak, wat ook al sy agtergrond is.
Dit is moontlik om deur godsdiens omring te wees en tog te mis wat God gesê het.
’n Nederige hart wat op God se Woord reageer, kan ’n geslag verander.

en.title: Nehemiah: Pray and Build
story: Nehemiah was the cupbearer to King Artaxerxes of Persia, a trusted position close to the most powerful man in the world. But when his brother brought news that Jerusalem’s walls were broken down and its gates burnt, Nehemiah ‘sat down and wept’. For days he mourned, fasted and prayed.

Four months later, the king noticed his sad face. That was dangerous; servants were expected to look happy in the king’s presence! When the king asked what he wanted, Nehemiah did something wonderful: ‘I prayed to the God of heaven, and I answered the king.’ A lightning-fast prayer in the middle of a conversation! The king gave him permission, letters and timber for the job.
In Jerusalem, Nehemiah inspected the walls secretly by night, then gathered the people: ‘Come, let us rebuild the wall.’ Families each took a section, often the part right next to their own homes.

Not everyone was happy. Sanballat and Tobiah mocked them: ‘Even a fox climbing up on it would break down their wall of stones!’ Later they plotted to attack. Nehemiah responded with prayer and wise planning: ‘We prayed to our God and posted a guard day and night.’ Half the workers held spears while the others built, and the builders wore swords at their sides.
‘Don’t be afraid of them,’ Nehemiah said. ‘Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome.’
The wall was finished in just fifty-two days. Even the enemies ‘realised that this work had been done with the help of our God’.
Nehemiah shows us that prayer and hard work go together. We pray as though everything depends on God, and we work faithfully with the strength He gives.

verse.text: The God of heaven will give us success. We His servants will start rebuilding.

lessons: Prayer and hard work go together.
We can pray quick prayers anytime, even in the middle of a conversation.
When people mock or oppose us, we remember how great God is.

af.title: Nehemia: Bid en Bou
story: Nehemia was die skinker van koning Artasasta van Persië, ’n betroubare posisie naby die magtigste man in die wêreld. Maar toe sy broer nuus bring dat Jerusalem se mure afgebreek en sy poorte afgebrand is, het Nehemia ‘gaan sit en gehuil’. Dae lank het hy getreur, gevas en gebid.

Vier maande later het die koning sy hartseer gesig opgemerk. Dit was gevaarlik; diensknegte moes gelukkig lyk in die koning se teenwoordigheid! Toe die koning vra wat hy wil hê, het Nehemia iets wonderliks gedoen: ‘Ek het tot die God van die hemel gebid, en ek het die koning geantwoord.’ ’n Blitsvinnige gebed in die middel van ’n gesprek! Die koning het hom toestemming, briewe en hout vir die werk gegee.

In Jerusalem het Nehemia die mure in die geheim snags ondersoek, en toe die mense bymekaargemaak: ‘Kom, laat ons die muur herbou.’ Families het elkeen ’n deel gevat, dikwels die stuk reg langs hulle eie huise.

Nie almal was gelukkig nie. Sanballat en Tobia het hulle gespot: ‘Selfs ’n jakkals wat daarop klim, sal hulle klipmuur afbreek!’ Later het hulle beplan om aan te val. Nehemia het met gebed en ’n wyse plan gereageer: ‘Ons het tot ons God gebid en dag en nag wagte uitgesit.’ Die helfte van die werkers het spiese vasgehou terwyl die ander gebou het, en die bouers het swaarde aan hulle sy gedra.
‘Moenie vir hulle bang wees nie,’ het Nehemia gesê. ‘Onthou die Here, wat groot en ontsagwekkend is.’
Die muur was in net twee-en-vyftig dae klaar. Selfs die vyande ‘het besef dat hierdie werk met die hulp van ons God gedoen is’.
Nehemia wys vir ons dat gebed en harde werk saamgaan. Ons bid asof alles van God afhang, en ons werk getrou met die krag wat Hy gee.

verse.text: Die God van die hemel sal ons laat slaag. Ons, sy dienaars, gaan begin herbou.

lessons: Gebed en harde werk gaan saam.
Ons kan enige tyd vinnige gebede bid, selfs in die middel van ’n gesprek.
As mense ons spot of teenstaan, onthou ons hoe groot God is.

en.title: Builders Who Pray
story: Nehemiah lived about 140 years after Jerusalem had been destroyed by Babylon. Some exiles had returned and rebuilt the temple, but the city walls still lay in ruins. In the ancient world a city without walls was defenceless and humiliated.

Nehemiah had a comfortable, influential job as the Persian king’s cupbearer. He could easily have said, ‘That’s sad, but it’s not my problem.’ Instead, the news broke his heart. Nehemiah 1 records his prayer. Notice its shape: he praises God’s greatness and faithfulness, confesses sin (including his own and his family’s), reminds God of His promises, and only then makes his request. Prayer for Nehemiah was not a last resort; it was the first thing he did.

For about four months he prayed, until the king noticed his sadness and asked what he wanted. Then comes one of the shortest prayers in the Bible: ‘Then I prayed to the God of heaven, and I answered the king.’ Long seasons of prayer had prepared him for that split-second moment.

Nehemiah also planned carefully. He asked for letters of safe passage and timber, he inspected the damage before announcing anything, and he organised families to rebuild the sections near their homes. Faith and wisdom were partners, not rivals.

Opposition came in waves: mockery (‘What are those feeble Jews doing?’), threats of attack, discouragement from within (‘The strength of the labourers is giving out’), and later, personal attacks and attempts to trick him. Each time Nehemiah responded with the same pattern: pray, plan and keep going. When enemies tried to lure him away, he answered: ‘I am carrying on a great project and cannot go down.’
The wall was completed in fifty-two days, and even the surrounding nations ‘realised that this work had been done with the help of our God’.
What is God asking you to build? Maybe a friendship, a habit, a skill or your faith itself. Pray first, plan wisely, expect opposition, and don’t come down from the wall.

af.title: Bouers wat Bid
story: Nehemia het omtrent 140 jaar nadat Jerusalem deur Babilon vernietig is, gelewe. Party ballinge het teruggekeer en die tempel herbou, maar die stadsmure het nog in puin gelê. In die antieke wêreld was ’n stad sonder mure weerloos en verneder.

Nehemia het ’n gemaklike, invloedryke werk as die Persiese koning se skinker gehad. Hy kon maklik gesê het: ‘Dis hartseer, maar dis nie my probleem nie.’ In plaas daarvan het die nuus sy hart gebreek. Nehemia 1 skryf sy gebed op. Let op die vorm daarvan: hy prys God se grootheid en trou, bely sonde (insluitend sy eie en sy familie s’n), herinner God aan sy beloftes, en eers dan maak hy sy versoek. Vir Nehemia was gebed nie ’n laaste uitweg nie; dit was die eerste ding wat hy gedoen het.

Omtrent vier maande lank het hy gebid, totdat die koning sy hartseer opgemerk en gevra het wat hy wil hê. Dan kom een van die kortste gebede in die Bybel: ‘Toe het ek tot die God van die hemel gebid, en ek het die koning geantwoord.’ Lang tye van gebed het hom voorberei vir daardie oomblik van ’n breukdeel van ’n sekonde.

Nehemia het ook versigtig beplan. Hy het vir briewe vir veilige deurgang en hout gevra, hy het die skade ondersoek voordat hy enigiets aangekondig het, en hy het families georganiseer om die dele naby hulle huise te herbou. Geloof en wysheid was vennote, nie teenstanders nie.

Teenstand het in golwe gekom: spot (‘Wat doen daardie swak Jode?’), dreigemente van aanvalle, moedeloosheid van binne (‘Die krag van die werkers raak op’), en later persoonlike aanvalle en pogings om hom te flous. Elke keer het Nehemia met dieselfde patroon gereageer: bid, beplan en hou aan. Toe vyande hom probeer weglok, het hy geantwoord: ‘Ek is besig met ’n groot werk en kan nie afkom nie.’
Die muur is in twee-en-vyftig dae voltooi, en selfs die nasies rondom ‘het besef dat hierdie werk met die hulp van ons God gedoen is’.
Wat vra God jou om te bou? Dalk ’n vriendskap, ’n gewoonte, ’n vaardigheid of jou geloof self. Bid eerste, beplan wys, verwag teenstand, en moenie van die muur afkom nie.

en.title: Nehemiah Builds the Wall
story: Nehemiah worked for a great king, far away from home. One day he heard sad news: the wall around Jerusalem, God’s city, was broken down, and its gates had been burnt. The people there were in danger.

Nehemiah sat down and cried. Then he prayed for days. When the king asked why he looked sad, Nehemiah said a quick prayer in his heart and then bravely asked, ‘Please may I go and rebuild the city?’ And the king said yes!
In Jerusalem, Nehemiah got everyone to help. Families worked side by side, each one fixing the part of the wall near their own house. Brick by brick, the wall grew.
But some enemies laughed at them. ‘That wall is so weak, even a fox could knock it down!’ they mocked. Later they planned to attack.
What did Nehemiah do? He prayed, and he made a plan. Half the people worked while the other half kept watch. ‘Don’t be afraid,’ he said. ‘Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome!’
In just fifty-two days, the wall was finished! Even the enemies could see that God had helped them.
When you have hard work to do, like a tricky puzzle, a tidy-up or something new to learn, you can pray and keep going. God will help you.

verse.text: The God of heaven will help us succeed.

lessons: God helps me do hard work when I pray.
I can pray quick prayers in my heart, anytime.
When people make fun of me, I can keep going with God.

What hard work do you need God’s help with?

thank you that you help me with hard things.

and help me keep going. Amen.

af.title: Nehemia Bou die Muur
story: Nehemia het vir ’n groot koning gewerk, ver weg van die huis af. Eendag het hy hartseer nuus gehoor: die muur om Jerusalem, God se stad, was afgebreek, en sy poorte was afgebrand. Die mense daar was in gevaar.

Nehemia het gaan sit en gehuil. Toe het hy dae lank gebid. Toe die koning vra hoekom hy hartseer lyk, het Nehemia ’n vinnige gebedjie in sy hart gebid en toe dapper gevra: ‘Mag ek asseblief gaan en die stad herbou?’ En die koning het ja gesê!
In Jerusalem het Nehemia almal gekry om te help. Families het langs mekaar gewerk, en elkeen het die deel van die muur naby hulle eie huis reggemaak. Steen vir steen het die muur gegroei.
Maar party vyande het vir hulle gelag. ‘Daardie muur is so swak, selfs ’n jakkals kan dit omstamp!’ het hulle gespot. Later het hulle beplan om aan te val.

Wat het Nehemia gedoen? Hy het gebid, en hy het ’n plan gemaak. Die helfte van die mense het gewerk terwyl die ander helfte wag gestaan het. ‘Moenie bang wees nie,’ het hy gesê. ‘Onthou die Here, wat groot en wonderlik is!’
In net twee-en-vyftig dae was die muur klaar! Selfs die vyande kon sien dat God hulle gehelp het.
As jy moeilike werk het om te doen, soos ’n moeilike legkaart, opruim of iets nuuts om te leer, kan jy bid en aanhou. God sal jou help.

verse.text: Die God van die hemel sal ons help om dit reg te kry.

lessons: God help my om moeilike werk te doen as ek bid.
Ek kan enige tyd vinnige gebedjies in my hart bid.
As mense my spot, kan ek saam met God aanhou.
questions: Wat het Nehemia gedoen toe die vyande vir hulle gelag het?
Met watter moeilike werk het jy God se hulp nodig?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U my met moeilike dinge help.
Help my asseblief met…
en help my om aan te hou. Amen.

mission.text: Bid môre, voordat jy iets moeiliks begin, ’n vinnige ‘Nehemia-gebed’: ‘God, help my asseblief!’

en.title: Campfire Night: Valley of Courage
story: Welcome to the second campfire of the Trail of the Living Water! This week you walked through the Valley of Courage with Deborah, who listened to God and went into battle; Gideon, the hero in hiding; three hundred men with torches in clay jars; Hannah, who poured out her heart; Josiah, the young king who found God’s Word; and Nehemiah, who prayed and built. None of them were brave on their own. Their courage came from God being with them, and so can yours.

en.title: Campfire Night: Valley of Courage
story: This week you met six people who faced impossible situations: an army of iron chariots, years of raids, an enemy like locusts, a longing that would not go away, a nation that had lost God’s Word, and a city in ruins. Not one of them was naturally fearless. Barak hesitated, Gideon hid, Hannah wept, Josiah grieved and Nehemiah was afraid in front of the king. But each one discovered that God goes ahead, calls us by who we will become, wins by His Spirit, hears our deepest prayers, uses the young and helps the builder. Courage is not the absence of fear. It is trusting God more than our fear.

af.title: Kampvuuraand: Vallei van Moed
story: Welkom by die tweede kampvuur van Die Pad van die Lewende Water! Hierdie week het ons deur die Vallei van Moed gestap. Ons het Debora ontmoet, wat God vertrou het om voor te gaan; Gideon, wat weggekruip het toe God hom ’n dapper held noem; driehonderd mans met trompette en fakkels; Hanna, wat haar hart uitgestort het; Josia, die seunkoning wat God se Woord gekry het; en Nehemia, wat gebid en gebou het. Kom ons onthou wat ons oor God ontdek het.
af.game: Dapper muur: bou ’n muur met blokke, boeke of kussings. Noem elke keer as jy ’n steen byvoeg een dapper ding wat jy met God se hulp kan doen.
questions: Soos watter dapper persoon van hierdie week wil jy wees?
Wat is een dapper ding wat jy hierdie week gedoen het?
prayer: Liewe God,
U gaan voor my uit, U noem my dapper,
U hoor my gebede,
en U help my met moeilike dinge. Dankie! Amen.

mission.text: Leer hierdie week se Skatvers, Sagaria 4:6, en sê dit vir iemand in jou familie.

af.journal: Teken ’n muur van ses stene, en skryf op elke steen een skat oor God van hierdie week.

blurb.en: A king asks for wisdom, ravens deliver dinner, God whispers, an invisible army appears, and empty jars overflow.
blurb.af: ’n Koning vra vir wysheid, kraaie bring aandete, God fluister, ’n onsigbare leër verskyn, en leë kanne loop oor.

en.text: If any of you lacks wisdom, ask God, who gives generously to all.

af.text: As iemand van julle wysheid kortkom, moet hy dit van God vra, wat aan almal mildelik gee.

trait.en: God gives wisdom when I ask
trait.af: God gee wysheid as ek vra

trait.en: God speaks in a gentle whisper
trait.af: God praat met ’n sagte fluistering

trait.en: God protects me more than I can see
trait.af: God beskerm my meer as wat ek kan sien

trait.af: God vul leë plekke

trait.af: God het mag oor die lewe

blurb.en: Water becomes wine, a roof gets opened, a trembling hand touches a cloak, and Jesus teaches us how to love and how to pray.
blurb.af: Water word wyn, ’n dak word oopgemaak, ’n bewende hand raak aan ’n mantel, en Jesus leer ons hoe om lief te hê en hoe om te bid.

en.text: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.

af.text: Jesus Christus is gister en vandag dieselfde, en tot in ewigheid.

trait.en: Jesus brings joy and does the impossible
trait.af: Jesus bring vreugde en doen die onmoontlike

trait.en: Jesus forgives and heals
trait.af: Jesus vergewe en genees

trait.en: Jesus notices me in the crowd
trait.af: Jesus sien my raak in die skare

trait.en: Jesus teaches me to love everyone
trait.af: Jesus leer my om almal lief te hê

trait.en: God is our Father who loves to hear us
trait.af: God is ons Vader wat ons graag hoor

blurb.en: A thirsty woman, two busy sisters, a friend raised from the grave, a towel and a basin, a vine, and a prayer Jesus prayed for you.
blurb.af: ’n Dors vrou, twee besige susters, ’n vriend wat uit die graf opgewek word, ’n handdoek en ’n skottel, ’n wynstok, en ’n gebed wat Jesus vir jou gebid het.

en.text: Whoever drinks the water I give them will never thirst.

af.text: Wie van die water drink wat Ek hom sal gee, sal nooit weer dors kry nie.

trait.en: Jesus satisfies my thirsty heart
trait.af: Jesus les my dors hart

trait.en: Being with Jesus matters most
trait.af: Om by Jesus te wees, is die belangrikste

trait.en: Jesus is the resurrection and the life
trait.af: Jesus is die opstanding en die lewe

trait.en: Jesus serves, and teaches me to serve
trait.af: Jesus dien, en leer my om te dien

trait.en: I grow by staying close to Jesus
trait.af: Ek groei deur naby Jesus te bly

trait.en: Jesus prays for me
trait.af: Jesus bid vir my

blurb.en: A beggar leaps up, a brave martyr forgives, a traveller is baptised, an enemy is changed, and prison doors open.
blurb.af: ’n Bedelaar spring op, ’n dapper martelaar vergewe, ’n reisiger word gedoop, ’n vyand word verander, en tronkdeure gaan oop.

en.text: I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God that brings salvation to everyone who believes.

af.text: Ek skaam my nie oor die evangelie nie, want dit is ’n krag van God tot redding vir elkeen wat glo.

trait.en: There is power in the name of Jesus

trait.en: God sends me to share the good news

trait.en: Nobody is too far for God to change
trait.af: Niemand is te ver vir God om te verander nie

trait.en: God answers when His people pray together
trait.af: God antwoord wanneer sy mense saam bid

trait.en: I can praise God even in hard times
trait.af: Ek kan God selfs in moeilike tye prys

blurb.en: How do God’s children live? Growing fruit, wearing God’s armour, loving like Jesus, using our gifts, and looking forward to a world made new.
blurb.af: Hoe lewe God se kinders? Ons laat vrugte groei, dra God se wapenrusting, het lief soos Jesus, gebruik ons gawes, en sien uit na ’n wêreld wat nuut gemaak word.

af.text: Lewe as kinders van die lig.

trait.en: The Holy Spirit grows good fruit in me
trait.af: Die Heilige Gees laat goeie vrugte in my groei

trait.en: God makes me strong in His power

trait.en: God’s kind of love never fails
trait.af: God se soort liefde vergaan nooit

trait.af: God gee my gawes om ander te help

trait.en: God will make everything new
